stories.title: VIDEO | Meerut SSP slaps protesters:Lawyer attempts suicide inside police van; cops lathicharge, assault detainees
stories.summary: A protest demanding justice for BA student Lalita Gautam turned violent in Meerut on Wednesday after police used a lathi-charge to disperse demonstrators outside the Collectorate. Around 50 to 60 people were detained after protesters blocked the road while attempting to submit a memorandum to the District Magistrate (DM). The demonstration lasted for nearly three hours after police shut the Collectorate's main gate as a large crowd gathered. Protesters alleged that Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Avinash Pandey assaulted demonstrators, including people inside a police van. During the detention, a lawyer allegedly attempted suicide inside the police vehicle by making a noose from a towel. Police maintained that the road blockade had caused severe traffic disruption and said force was used to restore law and order. See 2 pictures- Protest over Lalita Gautam's murder The protest was organised by members of the Dalit community over the murder of Lalita Gautam, a third-year BA student who was killed in May. Congress leader Hemant Pradhan, members of the Dalit community and representatives of several social organisations joined the demonstration. Although the protesters had initially been allowed to submit a memorandum, police closed the Collectorate gate after large numbers of people arrived from Meerut, Noida, Ghaziabad and nearby districts. The protesters then staged a sit-in outside the gate, blocking traffic. Senior police officers urged the crowd to clear the road and submit the memorandum peacefully, but the protesters refused to disperse. Police action and allegations After nearly three hours, police carried out a lathi-charge to clear the protest site. Protesters alleged that they were abused and assaulted during the operation and claimed SSP Avinash Pandey entered a police van and assaulted those taken into custody. Among those detained were several political and community leaders, including Congress leader Hemant Pradhan. Police said cases had been registered against around 20 people in connection with the protest. Advocate Ravi Gautam, who had travelled from Noida, alleged that he was assaulted while in police custody and later attempted suicide inside the police van. A video of the incident has surfaced. Police, however, said Ravi Gautam and another protester, Digvijay Bhati, already faced several criminal cases and accused them of attempting to disrupt public order. They said further legal action would be taken against them. Police response and protesters' demands SSP Avinash Pandey said the Lalita Gautam murder case had already been solved and that the main accused, along with two alleged accomplices, had been arrested. He said police had remained in contact with the victim's family and alleged that some people had incited the family to organise the road blockade. He added that police had repeatedly appealed to protesters to clear the road before using force to restore traffic and law and order. The protesters demanded the arrest of all those involved in the murder, a fast-track trial, the death penalty for the accused, financial compensation for the victim's family and a government job for one family member. Akhilesh Yadav criticises police Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav criticised the police action, sharing a video that allegedly showed officers assaulting protesters inside a police vehicle. He accused the BJP government of suppressing voices demanding justice for Lalita Gautam and described the lathi-charge as unacceptable. Background of the murder case Lalita Gautam went missing on 15 May after leaving home to appear for an examination. Her body was recovered two days later from a sugarcane field in Rohta police station limits. Following allegations of gang rape and murder by her family, police registered a case against three men. During the investigation, the main accused, Ankush, was arrested. Police allege he confessed that he had known Lalita for three years and suspected she was in contact with another man, leading to a dispute that culminated in her murder with the help of his associates. All the accused have since been arrested, but members of the Dalit community continue to demand the harshest punishment and speedy justice.

stories.title: Gorakhpur to launch ₹80 crore municipal bond:Funds will build commercial complex, launch expected by the end of August
stories.summary: The Gorakhpur Municipal Corporation (GMC) is preparing to launch its first municipal bond worth nearly ₹80 crore to raise funds for infrastructure development and strengthen its financial independence. Following approval from the Uttar Pradesh government, the civic body has accelerated the process. If everything proceeds as planned, the bond is expected to be launched in the last week of August. ₹79.94 crore bond with 10-year maturity The corporation plans to issue a ₹79.94 crore municipal bond with a 10-year maturity period. Initially, only SEBI-listed companies will be eligible to invest in the bond. The coupon rate (interest rate) is yet to be finalized. For credit assessment, the corporation has appointed India Ratings and CARE Ratings as the credit rating agencies. Funds to build commercial-cum-residential complex The money raised through the bond will be used to develop a modern multi-storey commercial-cum-residential complex at the Jal Kal campus in Golghar. The project will include shops, office spaces, and residential flats, which will be leased or rented out. The civic body expects the project to generate a steady annual income, creating a sustainable financial base for future development projects. Rental income to repay bond The Municipal Corporation plans to repay both the interest and principal of the bond using rental income generated from the complex, along with other revenue sources. If the project fails to generate the expected income, repayments will be made through the corporation's other revenue streams. Move expected to strengthen city's financial capacity Officials believe the bond issuance will significantly improve the corporation's financial strength and make it easier to raise funds from the market for future infrastructure projects. The initiative is expected to support greater investment in roads, sanitation, street lighting, drainage, and other civic infrastructure across the city. What is a municipal bond? A municipal bond is a financial instrument through which a municipal corporation raises money from investors for public infrastructure projects. In return, investors receive periodic interest payments, while the principal amount is repaid upon maturity. Municipal bonds are issued under regulations prescribed by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). Launch preparations in final stage Municipal Commissioner Ajay Jain said preparations for the bond issuance are progressing rapidly. While the maturity period and credit rating agencies have been finalised, a decision on the coupon rate will be taken soon. He expressed confidence that the Gorakhpur Municipal Corporation's first municipal bond will be launched by the end of August, calling it a major financial milestone for the city.

stories.title: Raid at retired UP ARTO's house:Team seizes 13 kg gold, 9 kg silver; ₹1.62 crore cash found hidden in walls and packets
stories.summary: Vigilance officials raided the Lucknow residence of retired Assistant Regional Transport Officer (ARTO) Lalit Kumar in Uttar Pradesh. During the raid, which lasted nearly 26 hours, officials recovered 13kg of gold, 9kg of silver and diamond jewellery from his home. The seized valuables are estimated to be worth ₹20 crore. Documents relating to 15 properties, including houses, flats and agricultural land, were also found. Vigilance officials estimated the total value of the recovered assets at around ₹35 crore Action continued for two days, cash was hidden in various places in the house The Vigilance team raided the C-143 residence in Chandralok Colony, Aliganj, on July 7 and 8, with a search warrant from the court. During the search, approximately ₹1.62 crore in cash, hidden in packets in different parts of the house, were recovered. Additionally, a large quantity of gold and silver biscuits and jewelry were also found. 13 kg gold, 9 kg silver, and jewelry worth crores The gold and silver found during the search were evaluated by a government-approved valuer. Approximately 13 kg of gold and about 9 kg of silver were recovered during the investigation, with an estimated value of around ₹20 crore. Properties worth crores in Lucknow, Noida and Barabanki During the investigation, documents for houses, plots, and agricultural land were found in several areas of Lucknow, including Aliganj, Vrindavan Yojana, Ismailganj, Mohanlalganj, and Balganj. Additionally, bookings for two flats in Noida and land documents in Barabanki and Raebareli were also recovered. The estimated value of these immovable properties is said to be around ₹13 crore. Cars, weapons and investments worth over ₹1 crore During the search, vigilance also found a Toyota Innova and a Hyundai i20 car, a revolver, and documents of investments exceeding ₹1 crore in banks, post offices, mutual funds, and fixed deposits. Evidence of heavy expenditure on home decor and expensive household items have also been found. Investigation underway in disproportionate assets case A case was registered against Lalit Kumar under the Prevention of Corruption Act after an investigation by the UP Vigilance Establishment. During the investigation, upon finding evidence of disproportionate assets, action was taken by obtaining a search warrant from the court. Team to receive ₹1 lakh reward According to the Vigilance Establishment, all recovered assets and investments are being verified and included in the investigation. For this successful operation, the Director General of Police and Director, Vigilance Establishment, have announced a reward of ₹1 lakh to the Lucknow sector team.

stories.title: Police officer suspended over rape allegation:Woman claims he forced her into a live-in relationship and later an abortion
stories.summary: A woman in Bareilly has accused a sub-inspector of rape and assault, alleging he exploited her after she approached a police station to complain about a dispute with her husband. According to the woman, the officer initially showed sympathy before promising to marry her and help her secure a job. She alleged that he told her, "You are very beautiful, I will leave my wife for you," and kept her with him for nearly a year by repeatedly assuring her that they would marry. On Tuesday at around 4 pm, the woman reached the Senior Superintendent of Police's office and demanded that an FIR be registered against the sub-inspector, as well as his wife and sons. The SSP said the complaint is under investigation. The sub-inspector has been suspended pending the inquiry. Woman reached the police station after a fight with her husband The woman, a resident of Baradari police station area, said - I have been having disputes with my husband since 2022. I am living separately from my husband. In 2025, I went to Baradari police station with a complaint against my husband and in-laws. There, I met Sub-Inspector (Daroga) Naresh Babu, who was posted at the police station. The sub-inspector first listened to my problem, then assured me of help. He claimed that he had a good hold in the police department. Due to direct connections with the captain, he could get me a job. Along with this, he also promised to divorce his wife and marry me. Now read the woman's allegations Made relations by luring with marriage: After assuring marriage, Sub-inspector Naresh Babu started staying in contact with me. He also started coming and going to my house. Later, he had physical relations with me several times. I kept trusting the sub-inspector's words, because I believed he would marry me. Since last year's Karwa Chauth, Sub-inspector Naresh Babu started living with me at my house. Took jewellery worth 8 lakhs by making an excuse of son's marriage: In February 2026, Sub-inspector Naresh Babu, citing his son's marriage, took gold jewellery worth about 8 lakh rupees from me. Later, when I asked for the jewellery back, he started procrastinating. When I protested, he started threatening me. Forced Abortion: Meanwhile, I became pregnant. When the sub-inspector found out about this, he forcibly made me take abortion pills on May 12. After taking the medicine, my health deteriorated. Due to this, I had to be admitted to the hospital. Arrived home with wife and sons, assaulted: On May 23, Sub-Inspector Naresh Babu arrived home with his wife and sons. He also abused and assaulted me. Upon this, I informed Dial-112. However, before the police arrived, they fled after threatening to kill me. Sub-inspector's family behaved rudely: On the night of July 4/5, the sub-inspector was injured in a road accident. Upon learning this, I admitted him to the hospital and also bore the cost of treatment. The next day, his family members behaved rudely with me at the hospital. Additionally, the sub-inspector also ended his relationship with me. Showed police authority: The sub-inspector intimidated and threatened me by citing his influence and connections in the police department. He said that he himself is a policeman. No action will be taken against me. Because of this, I could not gather the courage to complain for a long time.

stories.title: Raids on properties of former SP MLA close to Akhilesh:ED carries out searches in suspected money laundering case
stories.summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) raided three properties belonging to former SP MLA Deep Narayan Singh Yadav on Wednesday morning. The ED reached a flat of the former MLA in Jhansi and two in Lucknow at 7 AM. The ED is investigating Deep Narayan's properties and financial transactions in a suspected money laundering case. The former MLA has an ancestral home in Moon City, Jhansi. Simultaneously, two flats located in Eldeco Colony and Sunrise Apartment on Kanpur Road in Lucknow were raided. According to sources, the raiding team comprised more than 20 officers and staff. Force was deployed outside all three locations. No one is being allowed to enter or exit. Deep Narayan is close to SP chief Akhilesh Yadav. Sources claimed that a raid also took place at the residence of a close relative of Deep Narayan. Full details related to the raid have not yet emerged. Two pictures of the ED raid Former MLA's whereabouts not clear Sources said that the ED team is searching room by room and family members present were interrogated. However, it is not yet clear where the former MLA was during the raid. According to sources, this action by the ED has been taken on the basis of an FIR by the Uttar Pradesh Vigilance Establishment. It is being said that 23 FIRs are registered against the former MLA. An extortion and robbery case was registered on 20 November On 20 November 2025, Prem Singh Paliwal, a resident of Bhujond village, accused Deep Narayan and his associate Anil Yadav, a resident of Akhadapura, of robbery and extortion. An FIR was registered against them at Moth Police Station the same day. Police announced a ₹25,000 reward for information leading to Anil Yadav's arrest. On 12 December, Anil Yadav surrendered before the court. ₹25,000 reward announced for Deep Narayan Meanwhile, Deep Narayan remained absconding and police continued searching for him. He filed a bail plea before the Jhansi court, but it was rejected. Following the court's order, property worth ₹20 crore belonging to Deep Narayan was attached on 13 December. Police had also announced a ₹25,000 reward for information leading to his arrest. Reached court on a motorbike to surrender He filed another application to surrender before the court on 15 December but did not appear, seeking another date through his lawyer. The court granted him time until 20 December. On 20 December, he arrived at the court riding pillion on the motorbike of his lawyer, Zahid Mansoori. He surrendered before the court, which subsequently remanded him to 14 days in judicial custody. Later, police sought eight hours of custody to recover the looted money, but the court granted six hours instead. Police claimed recovery of ₹15,000 from his house After securing custody, police took him to Budhawali village in Moth, his ancestral village. They claimed to have recovered ₹15,000 in cash, allegedly part of the robbery proceeds, from his house. He was then taken back to jail, where he remained lodged. Last seen at a press conference yesterday He was granted bail by the court on 7 May. Since then, he had been staying at his residence in Moon City. On Tuesday, Ballia-based leader Sanatan Pandey visited Jhansi and addressed a press conference at the Circuit House. Deep Narayan was also present at the event. stories.title: NIA raids cosmetic trader's home over terror funding:Agency raids premises of 3 brothers; cash-counting machine brought in during search
stories.summary: The National Investigation Agency (NIA), assisted by local police and central security forces, carried out simultaneous raids on Wednesday (8 July) morning at the homes of cosmetics businessman Abdul Qadir and his two brothers in Bulandshahr. The trio is under investigation for alleged hawala transactions, terror funding and money laundering. Teams that reportedly arrived from Visakhapatnam in three vehicles launched coordinated searches at all three properties in the city's Intarodi locality at around 8.30 am. The searches are still underway at the time of reporting, with officials said to have recovered a large quantity of cash from the residences of Abdul Qadir, Faisal and Bilal. Cash counting machines brought in as searches continue According to reports, currency counting machines were requisitioned from banks to process the recovered cash. Police personnel from two police stations have been deployed at the site while the counting operation continues. Security agencies have sealed off the Intarodi neighbourhood and adjoining areas, restricting all movement. Outsiders have been barred from entering the locality, while those already inside the raided premises have not been allowed to leave until the operation is completed. See pictures... Acting on intelligence inputs, the NIA launched coordinated searches at his residence and other linked locations. The search operation is being conducted under the supervision of two magistrates, with officials continuing to examine evidence at the raided premises”.

stories.title: UP teachers to receive accident insurance cover upto ₹1cr:State also launches ₹5 lakh cashless healthcare scheme
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday announced a comprehensive insurance and healthcare package for teachers and education department employees. The scheme includes accident insurance of up to ₹1 crore and cashless medical treatment of up to ₹5 lakh for nearly 12 lakh teachers across the state. Speaking at an event on Wednesday morning, the Chief Minister said that permanent teachers and employees will receive ₹10 lakh under Group Term Insurance, ₹1 crore Personal Accident Cover, ₹1 crore Permanent Disability Cover, and up to ₹1.60 crore Air Accident Insurance Cover in the event of an accident. He added that contractual employees earning more than ₹10,000 per month will also be covered, with personal accident insurance ranging from ₹30 lakh to ₹80 lakh. Employees earning less than ₹10,000 per month will receive ₹2 lakh accident insurance cover. Yogi said the scheme also provides financial support for the education of employees' children and the marriage of their daughters if a teacher or employee dies in an accident. He described the initiative as a first-of-its-kind programme, saying Uttar Pradesh is the first state to introduce such comprehensive protection for teachers. The Chief Minister also launched a cashless healthcare scheme providing treatment worth up to ₹5 lakh for around 12 lakh teachers. He said the state government will bear the entire annual cost of approximately ₹450 crore, with no contribution required from teachers. "We do not want anything from you except Guru Dakshina," Yogi said. “Our only expectation is that you focus on educating children. Schools should have a clean, positive environment that helps shape the country's future.” Before the event, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was welcomed with Vedic chants by 51 young priests (Batuks). He also visited an exhibition put up by schoolchildren. Looking at a telescope model, he jokingly asked a student, "Can this telescope show me the ministers sitting in Lucknow from here?" The Chief Minister had first announced the insurance scheme on Teachers' Day in 2025. The benefits will be extended to teachers, Shiksha Mitras, instructors, cooks and hostel wardens. Addressing the gathering, Secondary Education Minister Gulab Devi praised the Chief Minister and said that no one involved in the alleged theft of offerings at the Ram Mandir would be spared. She said the Chief Minister had constituted a committee to investigate the case, ensuring that no matter how influential or senior a person might be, they would not escape action. According to her, the move has been widely appreciated not only in Uttar Pradesh but across the country. Referring to the 2025–26 board examinations, Gulab Devi said that around 5.4 million students appeared for the exams and no cases of cheating were reported. She credited the state government's strict measures, saying they were so effective that cheating mafias did not dare to interfere and no examination papers were leaked.

stories.title: Police take 3 Ram Mandir donation theft accused into remand:CCTV shows them pocketing donation cash; Govind Dev meets Champat Rai
stories.summary: Ayodhya Ram Mandir donation theft case accused Lavkush Mishra, Anukalp Mishra and Karunesh Pandey have been taken into 40-hour police remand. A police team reached Faizabad Jail at 7:36 am on Wednesday and took the three accused to the Police Lines. According to the SIT report, CCTV footage shows the trio allegedly pocketing currency notes. Meanwhile, Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust Treasurer Swami Govind Dev Giri has reached to meet Champat Rai. Rai is staying in seclusion at Teerth Kshetra Puram near the Ram Mandir in Ramkot. On Tuesday, he broke his silence through a letter, saying all allegations against him are false. The SIT has also begun examining expenses related to major events organised by the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. Investigators are scrutinising bills and vouchers for the Ram Mandir consecration ceremony held on 22 January 2024 and the flag-hoisting ceremony on 25 November 2025. Records show ₹113 crore was spent on the consecration ceremony, attended by around 8,000 guests, while ₹10.12 crore was spent on the flag-hoisting event.

stories.title: Heavy rain sweeps across 10 UP cities:Delivery boy swept into drain in Mathura, 68 cities remain on alert
stories.summary: The monsoon has gathered pace in Uttar Pradesh. Rain is falling in 10 cities, including Mathura and Ghaziabad, on Wednesday morning. In Hathras, heavy rain has left roads submerged in waist-deep water. The current is so strong that cars and motorbikes are being swept away. Cloud cover persists across most districts of the state, while light winds have made conditions more humid. The weather department has issued a rain alert for 68 districts today, with 12 of them likely to receive heavy rainfall. On Tuesday, rain lashed 50 cities, including Lucknow and Prayagraj, from the morning onwards. In Mathura, overflowing drains swept away a delivery rider along with his motorbike. Local residents managed to pull him to safety. Sonbhadra recorded the highest rainfall in the past 24 hours at 31 mm, which is 195% above the normal 10.5 mm. Despite the recent showers, Uttar Pradesh has received 45% less rainfall than normal since 1 June.

stories.title: File Income Tax return by 31st July to avoid penalty:Check your ITR refund status in mins, filing is easier than before; CA not required
stories.summary: The last date for filing the Income Tax Return (ITR) is July 31. If you don't file an ITR within the stipulated time, you may have to pay a late fee of ₹1 thousand on annual income up to ₹5 lakh and up to ₹5 thousand on income exceeding ₹5 lakh. The Income Tax Department has made the ITR filing process much easier through the e-filing portal. Now you can easily file ITR yourself from home. The purpose is that people don't have to depend only on Chartered Accountants (CA) every time for filing returns. First, understand the new and old tax regimes According to Chartered Accountant Deepak Tiwari, if you are filing ITR for Assessment Year 2026-27, first know that the new tax regime is now the default. If you don't choose any option, the system will automatically put you in the new tax regime. Therefore, it is important to know which regime to choose. In the new regime, income tax is zero on income up to ₹12 lakh In the new tax system, the government has increased the scope of tax exemption. Now there is no direct tax on income up to ₹4 lakh. After this, if your total taxable income is up to ₹12 lakh, then the government gives a tax rebate of up to ₹60,000 under Section 87A. Due to this, your entire tax is waived, and you don't have to pay any tax. Apart from this, salaried people also get a standard deduction of ₹75 thousand. This means if your annual salary is up to ₹12.75 lakh, then after the standard deduction, your taxable income remains ₹12 lakh. In such a case, you get the benefit of a rebate, and your tax becomes zero. Now know about the old tax system If you choose the old tax regime, there is no tax on income up to ₹2.5 lakh. On taxable income up to ₹5 lakh, a rebate of ₹12,500 is available under Section 87A. Therefore, no tax needs to be paid. In this regime, you can avail tax exemption benefits like 80C, 80D, HRA. Now, file ITR from home Show different incomes in ITR like this House Rent: According to tax consultant Vinay Tiwari, income from rent must be shown under Income from House Property. The government directly provides a 30% standard deduction on total rent. This means if you receive ₹1 lakh as rent annually, tax will be levied only on ₹70 thousand. If there is a home loan on the same property, an additional exemption of up to ₹2 lakh can be availed on its interest. Bank Interest: Every interest received from bank accounts or FDs must be filled under Income from Other Sources, as it is already recorded in your AIS. Under the old tax regime, common people get an exemption of up to ₹10,000 on savings account interest under Section 80TTA. Meanwhile, senior citizens get an exemption of up to ₹50,000 in total on interest from both FDs and savings under Section 80TTB. Shares and Mutual Funds: Many people think that all data related to shares and mutual funds gets automatically filled in the ITR. Actually, AIS only shows purchase-sale information; you have to calculate the tax yourself. For this, you need to download the Capital Gains Statement from your broker (Zerodha or Groww) and fill in the information yourself. Dividend received from shares must also be shown in Income from Other Sources. Refund not coming? This could be the reason If the refund is not coming after filing the ITR, first check your bank account. Your bank account should be pre-validated on the income tax portal. Also, the name registered in the bank account and the information provided on the PAN portal should match completely. If this is not the case, even after the refund is approved, the money will not come to your account and may get stuck. If tax is zero in Form-16, is it still necessary to file ITR? If Form-16 shows zero tax, don't assume that there's no need to file ITR. Filing ITR depends on whether your total income and financial transactions fall under the rules set by the Income Tax Department. In some cases, filing ITR is mandatory even if no tax is payable. If a taxpayer passes away, will ITR need to be filed? Yes, the legal heir will have to register themselves as a Legal Heir on the income tax portal. For this, they will need to upload the death certificate, PAN, and other necessary documents. After approval, they will file the ITR on behalf of the deceased. If a refund is due, it will come to the verified bank account of the legal heir. According to the Supreme Court, if in the future a person dies in a road accident or becomes permanently disabled, the ITR will be an important basis for determining the compensation amount to be given to their family. In the case of businesspersons, the compensation will be calculated based on the average income of the ITR for the last 3 years.

stories.title: Ram Mandir treasurer says he is 'ashamed' over donation theft:Member claims more accused are involved; exact amount cannot be determined
stories.summary: After the case of theft of offerings at Ram Mandir came to light, the Trust is now preparing for major changes. Swami Govind Dev Giri, the treasurer of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, says that the mistake that happened will not be allowed to happen again. For this, the temple's system will be strengthened. An experienced CEO will be appointed. In a special conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, Swami Govind Dev provided important information regarding the Trust's meeting on July 22, the SIT investigation, and new arrangements for the temple. Read Swami Govind Dev's full interview A new CEO will be appointed to handle administrative arrangements Question- What changes are being made to the temple's management? Govind Dev- Changes in the temple's management and making it better have now become very necessary. We have also fully understood this. To ensure that the mistake made once does not happen again, improvements are being made in all departments. A CEO will be appointed to oversee the entire system and maintain administrative discipline. Question- Why is a CEO needed? Can't the trust members handle this responsibility? Govind Dev- All our trustees and workers are not sufficient to manage such a large system with administrative efficiency and strictness. Therefore, the need for a professional CEO was felt. Question- How and when will the CEO be appointed? Govind Dev- For this, a committee of 3 members has been formed. The committee will interview several people and provide 3 names to the trust. After this, we will select one person from them. The CEO will constantly oversee the management, supervision, and improvement of the temple. The process of selecting the CEO will be completed before the meeting on July 22. This work will be done in a transparent and impartial manner. Question- Will the trust be run on an administrative model like Kashi Vishwanath Dham? Govind Dev- No, the trust will function as before. However, there is a lot of scope for improvement in the system and work will be done in that direction. Question- Is there a plan to change the bank for donations now? Govind Dev- No decision has been made on this yet. This matter will be considered when it comes up in the trust meeting. Big decisions can be made in the July 22 meeting Question- 2 members have resigned from the trust, 1 post is vacant. When will these be filled? Govind Dev- All such decisions are made in the trust meeting. The next meeting is on July 22, and a decision on this will be taken then. Question- You are the treasurer, but you don't always stay in Ayodhya. How will you monitor? Govind Dev- As I said before, this is why a full-time CEO is needed. He will work in Ayodhya at all times. He will manage the entire system according to our instructions and established discipline. The amount of the theft will be known after the SIT report comes Question- Did the trust members never get a hint of this theft? Govind Dev- Personally, I never got any such hint. Even if someone else had some information, it did not reach me. Question- What was Gopal Rao's role in the offering theft? Govind Dev- What his role was in the theft is a subject of SIT investigation. His responsibility was to coordinate the temple's worship, darshan arrangements, and other tasks. I cannot say anything about his role in the theft. Question- Is there a possibility of more people being involved besides the 8 accused? Govind Dev- This possibility cannot be ruled out. When these 8 people were doing all this, there must have been other people watching or assisting. Identifying them is the job of the SIT. Question- There was no account of the offerings. How will it be known how many crores were stolen? Govind Dev- There was an account of the offerings, but the money was removed before it could be recorded. Therefore, it is very difficult to ascertain the exact amount of the theft. Allegations of Conspiracy Against Tinnu Yadav Question - You have accused Tinnu Yadav of conspiracy, who are you hinting at? Govind Dev - Based on news reports in the media, I had said that several calls from outsiders were found on his mobile. This could be true or false. It is a very serious matter for a person who has been working for so many years to do something like this. Question- Nishikant Dubey alleged that there was a conversation between Akhilesh and Tinnu? Govind Dev- I cannot confirm the truth of this. The situation will only become clear after the final report of the SIT is released. Question- How did the accused become so powerful that they even deleted CCTV footage? Govind Dev- How they got so much freedom is a big question. There was not enough surveillance on them, which made this possible. Were the CCTV footage recovered or not? I do not have information about this. Read what Govind Dev Giri has stated so far After allegations of theft of offerings and financial irregularities at Ayodhya Ram Temple, the trust's treasurer, Govind Dev Giri, has been continuously in discussion. He has given several statements on this entire matter so far. Refused to Resign: When journalists questioned him about resignation and accountability, he became angry. He was even seen pulling the microphones of media personnel. He clearly stated - I will not resign, because I have done nothing wrong. Clarified His Role: Regarding the questions arising due to his position as treasurer, Govind Giri said that his responsibility is to manage the audited records of the trust. He stated that he is not directly involved in the daily cash counting or transaction process. Defended Champat Rai: Even before the SIT's preliminary report came out, Govind Giri described the theft of offerings as a 'Jaghanya Mahapaap'. However, he defended the trust's general secretary, Champat Rai, saying that he had no role in it. His only mistake was trusting the wrong person. Offerings declared safe: Govind Giri says that the 2,929 valuable items received as donations by the trust are completely safe. He also said that any donor who wishes can come and see them.

stories.title: FIR against SP MLA Amitabh Bajpai in Kanpur:Accused of celebrating Akhilesh Yadav's birthday at primary school without permission
stories.summary: Police have registered an FIR against SP MLA Amitabh Bajpai in connection with the celebration of SP chief Akhilesh Yadav's birthday at Parmat Primary School in Kanpur. The case was registered by Gwaltoli police on the complaint of the school's suspended headmaster. According to the complaint, the SP MLA organised the birthday celebration on the school premises without permission. It has also been alleged that although an MP was scheduled to distribute school uniforms to the children, Amitabh Bajpai distributed the uniforms instead. The school's headmaster had already been suspended over the incident. Following his complaint, police have now registered a case against the MLA. Birthday celebrated at school on July 1 On July 1, Amitabh Bajpai celebrated Akhilesh Yadav's birthday at Parmat Primary School in Kanpur. Photographs and videos of the event later went viral on social media. The following day, headmaster Naveen Kumar Tripathi was suspended over the incident. On Tuesday, suspended headmaster Naveen Kumar Tripathi lodged a complaint at Gwaltoli police station. He alleged that the SP MLA forcibly held Akhilesh Yadav's birthday celebration on the school premises without obtaining any official permission. He further claimed that Amitabh Bajpai distributed school uniforms to the children during the event. Based on the complaint, Gwaltoli police registered an FIR against the SP MLA. FIR registered under BNS Section 132 The FIR has been registered under Section 132 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with assaulting or using criminal force against a public servant to deter them from discharging official duties. The provision is intended to protect government employees while performing their official responsibilities. Police have begun an investigation into the entire matter.

stories.title: Akhilesh sends notice to Nishikant Dubey over Tinnu Yadav link:BJP MP says, 'File an FIR too, I will also go to court'
stories.summary: A political row has erupted between SP president Akhilesh Yadav and BJP MP Nishikant Dubey over Ramashankar Yadav alias Tinnu Yadav, the accused in the theft of offerings at the Ram Mandir. On Tuesday at 1:55 pm, Akhilesh Yadav, through SP state president K.K. Pal, sent a legal defamation notice to Nishikant Dubey. The notice relates to allegations that Akhilesh had spoken to Tinnu Yadav. The SP chief has described the allegations as completely false, baseless and malicious. Meanwhile, SP leaders lodged a complaint at Friends Colony police station in Etawah against Nishikant Dubey and several others for circulating social media posts claiming that Tinnu had spoken to Akhilesh Yadav. Responding to the complaint, Nishikant Dubey said- Under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Akhilesh Yadav himself will have to go to the police station and file a complaint. Follow the law. Akhilesh had warned Dubey to delete the X post Nishikant Dubey, the BJP MP from Godda in Jharkhand, had shared an X post on July 5 by Saravanna Prasad Balasubramaniam, claiming that Tinnu Yadav had been in regular contact with Akhilesh Yadav. The post cited an alleged police investigation and mobile call records. While sharing it, Dubey wrote- Wasn't Tinnu talking to Tipu? Akhilesh Yadav reacted strongly to the post and gave Dubey 10 minutes to delete it. He warned- The BJP MP should remove his false social media post within 10 minutes, otherwise a named FIR will be registered against him. Calling the allegation false propaganda, Akhilesh said it violated parliamentary traditions, public decency and the dignity of Lord Ram. He alleged that the BJP was attempting to defame the PDA alliance. Nishikant responds to Akhilesh's warning Nishikant Dubey also replied on X, writing- Hurry up, why are you so troubled? It's only a question, isn't it? Who ordered the firing on Ram devotees in 1990? I will go to court. Defamation notice demands apology and deletion of post The Samajwadi Party has now formally initiated legal proceedings by issuing a defamation notice. The notice asks Nishikant Dubey to remove the social media post and issue a public apology. It warns that if he fails to do so, further legal action will follow. Akhilesh Yadav has also warned others sharing similar posts to delete them and apologise. Pawan Pandey challenges BJP to produce evidence Former SP MLA from Ayodhya, Pawan Pandey, released a video stating that the theft allegations had already been proved, the accused had been jailed and trustees had been removed. He alleged that the BJP, RSS and VHP were now spreading false propaganda by claiming that Akhilesh Yadav had spoken to Tinnu Yadav. Pawan Pandey said- It is an open challenge. If there is proof of any phone conversation between Akhilesh Yadav and Tinnu Yadav, produce it. Otherwise, publicly apologise to Akhilesh Yadav. He added that politics should be based on facts and evidence rather than false allegations, and said he would retire from politics if BJP leaders proved their claim. Who is Tinnu Yadav? Ramashankar Yadav alias Tinnu Yadav was the driver of Champat Rai. He is a resident of Ayodhya and is currently in jail. According to the SIT report, Tinnu Yadav had control over the keys to the temple's donation boxes and access arrangements without any formal written authorisation. The report further stated that Manish Kumar Yadav was assigned donation-counting duties on Tinnu Yadav's recommendation and was later found to be involved in theft cases. The SIT described these lapses as a serious failure in the mandir's security arrangements.

stories.title: Lucknow named India's most walkable city:Tops survey among 12 major cities; Delhi ranks eighth
stories.summary: Lucknow has achieved a major milestone after being ranked the most walkable city among the 12 major cities surveyed in the State of Indian Streets Report 2026. The Vice-Chairman of the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) said the authority is continuously working to improve public infrastructure in line with people's needs. Facilities will be further enhanced through development projects and parks. Nearly 28% of roads and footpaths are pedestrian-friendly According to the report, 28% of Lucknow's roads and footpaths allow people to walk without obstruction. Bengaluru ranked second with 25.9%, followed by Hyderabad at 15.1% and Chennai at 13.9%. As part of the survey, 346 footpaths across Lucknow were inspected, of which 97 were rated as being in excellent condition. Well-developed footpaths helped secure top ranking The report attributes Lucknow's top position to its well-maintained footpaths and improved pedestrian infrastructure in areas such as Ambedkar Park Road, Lohia Path, Indira Nagar and Gomti Nagar. LDA Vice-Chairman Prathmesh Kumar said the authority's objective is to make Lucknow a safe, accessible and convenient city for pedestrians. Pedestrian facilities to remain a development priority He said the LDA is continuously upgrading footpaths, greenways, public spaces and other essential civic infrastructure. The authority will continue to prioritise pedestrian convenience in future urban development projects to ensure safer and more accessible streets across the city.

stories.title: School journeys to become safer:Drivers and conductors to receive training; strict action against safety violations
stories.summary: A major initiative is being launched in Gorakhpur to further strengthen the safety of schoolchildren. Under the programme, all school vehicle drivers and conductors in the district will receive specialised training to ensure children travel safely to and from school. The Secondary Education Department and the Traffic Department will jointly conduct the campaign, providing training on road safety, traffic regulations, handling emergency situations and ensuring the safe transportation of children. Preparations have been completed, and the campaign is expected to begin by the end of this month. Expert teams to visit every tehsil Under the plan, tehsil-wise teams will be formed according to a pre-scheduled programme. These teams will visit schools across the district to train drivers and conductors of school vehicles. The training will cover safe driving practices, routine vehicle inspections, compliance with prescribed speed limits, safe boarding and alighting of students, first aid, immediate response during accidents or emergencies, and adherence to traffic regulations. Only trained drivers and conductors to operate school vehicles As part of the campaign, all schools will be instructed to ensure that only drivers and conductors who have completed the mandatory safety training and meet all government-prescribed standards are assigned to school vehicles. The department aims to eliminate any scope for negligence in the operation of school transport. No compromise on children's safety The Secondary Education Department said that the safety of students remains its highest priority and that no negligence will be tolerated. To achieve this, the Education Department and the Transport Department will jointly implement the campaign on a large scale to ensure every school vehicle complies with safety standards, enabling children to travel safely between home and school.

stories.title: CM Yogi on a two-day tour to Varanasi:To offer prayers today, will launch cashless healthcare scheme for teachers tomorrow
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will arrive in Varanasi on Tuesday evening for a two-day visit. During his stay, he will attend the wedding of State Minister Dayashankar Mishra's son on Tuesday evening. On Wednesday, he will launch a cashless healthcare scheme for teachers. According to District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar, the Chief Minister is scheduled to land at the Police Line helipad after 6 pm on Tuesday. From there, he will proceed directly to Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham to offer prayers. After the visit to the temple, he will attend the wedding reception of State Minister Dayashankar Mishra 'Dayalu's' son, Animesh, at Hotel Lemon Tree in Rohania. He will stay overnight at the Circuit House. To launch cashless healthcare scheme on Wednesday The District Magistrate said that on Wednesday, the Chief Minister will inaugurate a cashless medical treatment scheme for teachers and Shiksha Mitras of the Basic and Secondary Education Department at Hastkala Sankul in Bara Lalpur. He will also transfer scholarship funds exceeding ₹1 crore directly into the bank accounts of students across the state through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system. Godowlia–Maidagin stretch declared a no-vehicle zone Following the programme, the Chief Minister will return to the Police Line before leaving for Vindhyachal in Mirzapur. In view of his visit, the road between Maidagin and Godowlia will remain a no-vehicle zone. No vehicles of any kind will be permitted on the stretch during the Chief Minister's movement. The traffic department has issued an advisory for commuters.

stories.title: Yogi attacks Opposition over Waqf land issue:Claims poor people's lands was grabbed, opposition changes colours like a chameleon
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday targeted the Indian National Congress and Samajwadi Party in Pratapgarh. He said that thousands of hectares of land were sold in the name of Waqf in the state and the country, while lands meant for the welfare of poor people were encroached upon. “Did SP-Congress ever raise their voice against this? No. Because their mouths get locked when it comes to Waqf,” the Chief Minister said. CM Yogi said, “The pain of the opposition is that where they wanted to see the Babri structure, a grand temple has now been built there. Looking at their double standards, it seems even a chameleon has started feeling ashamed of them, because they change colours faster than it does.” He said the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust is managing the construction and arrangements of the temple and nobody has the right to interfere in its functioning. CM Yogi inaugurated and laid the foundation stones of 111 projects worth ₹384 crore. He also honoured BPSC topper Shraddha Pandey on the stage. Read Yogi's 5 big statements- 1- ‘SP-Congress who shed tears in support of Babri structure have no right to speak’ The Chief Minister said these parties repeatedly raise the same old issues — dividing society in the name of caste and attacking faith. He said these are the only two issues left with SP and Congress today. “You have seen continuous attempts to attack India’s Sanatan faith. Remember, Congress leaders used to say that Lord Ram never existed and Lord Krishna never existed,” he said. He said those who shed crocodile tears in support of the Babri structure in Ayodhya are now changing colours and talking about faith. “They say that the faith of Ayodhya is being played with. I want to ask, what kind of interference is happening? If Ram devotees say their faith is connected with Ayodhya, they have every right to say so because their ancestors fought for Ram Janmabhoomi,” Yogi said. “But Congress does not have this right because it questioned even the existence of Lord Ram,” he added. 2- ‘How can SP, which fired bullets at Ram devotees, talk about faith?’ Yogi said, “The SP, which ordered firing on Ram devotees, how can it talk about faith today?” He alleged that these parties object to the redevelopment of Hindu religious sites but had no problem spending crores of rupees on boundary walls of graveyards. “The country will no longer fall for the deception of Congress and SP,” he said. The Uttar Pradesh government had formed an SIT to investigate matters related to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. Based on the preliminary report, the SIT registered an FIR and action was taken against those against whom evidence was found. “But Congress and Samajwadi Party do not say a single word about corruption in the name of Waqf,” Yogi said. He questioned whether Hindu sentiments were not hurt when illegal slaughterhouses were operating, cow smuggling was taking place, Ram devotees were fired upon, Lord Ram and Lord Krishna were described as imaginary, and restrictions were imposed on Kanwar Yatra. He said Congress and SP should answer all these questions. 3-'Opposition's pain that despite misinformation, crores of people are reaching Ayodhya' Yogi said SP had created an identity crisis for the youth of Uttar Pradesh and was now creating various controversies as elections approached. “The progress visible in Uttar Pradesh today, freedom from disturbances and the peaceful environment created here are not liked by these opposition parties. They also do not like respect for our heritage,” he said. He alleged that the opposition once again wants to divide society on caste lines. “We have to rise above this and move ahead on the path of development,” he said. He said Ayodhya now has four-lane roads, double railway lines and an international airport named after Maharishi Valmiki. A night shelter has also been built in the name of Nishadraj. “This is the pain of the opposition that despite their propaganda, crores of people are reaching Ayodhya,” he said. 4- ‘Earlier, some families controlled government jobs’ Yogi said he was happy that hundreds of youths from Pratapgarh were selected in nearly 60,000 Uttar Pradesh Police recruitments. He said candidates from Pratapgarh are continuously getting selected in results announced by the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission and the Subordinate Services Selection Commission. “Earlier, some families had control over government jobs. There was no transparency, due to which youths of Pratapgarh were deprived of these opportunities,” he said. He added that when youths are deprived of opportunities, they migrate and the state suffers. “This was the reason why Uttar Pradesh was once called a ‘Bimaru state’,” Yogi said. 5- ‘Whenever religion and nation faced a crisis, Pratapgarh never stepped back’ Yogi said Pratapgarh has great mythological and historical importance. “Whenever religion and the nation faced a crisis, Pratapgarh never stepped back. During the First War of Independence in 1857, Babu Gulab Singh raised the first call for revolt from this land,” he said. He said the warriors of Pratapgarh shook the foundations of foreign rule. He added that Pratapgarh has earned global recognition due to the sweetness and quality of its amla. “We started the ‘One District, One Product’ scheme in 2018, but Pratapgarh had already proved its talent before that,” he said. Yogi said those who could not even imagine before 2017 that a medical college would come up in Pratapgarh can now see the Dr Sonelal Patel Government Medical College functioning there. He added that a nursing college is also being built in the district. “Daughters of Pratapgarh will receive nursing education here and contribute to the health sector through their services in India and across the world,” he said. The Chief Minister said he got the opportunity to inaugurate and lay foundation stones of development projects related to both assembly constituencies. Recalling his previous visit, he said MLA Rajendra Maurya had complained about several pending works. “I told him — brother, all works will be completed, just feed me rasmalai one day,” Yogi said.

stories.title: Champat Rai's first statement on Ram Mandir donation theft:Shares letter, promise to answer all allegations after SIT submits its final report
stories.summary: Former Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust General Secretary Champat Rai, who is facing allegations in the Ram Mandir donation theft case, broke his silence for the first time on Tuesday. He posted a handwritten letter addressed to Lord Ram's devotees on his X account. Champat Rai began the letter with a verse from the Shri Ramcharitmanas, 'Dheeraj dharam mitra aru naari, aapad kaal parikhiyehin chaari', and said that since 2024, several allegations had been levelled against him over the alleged theft of donations during the counting of offerings. He added that he had deliberately chosen to remain silent. He said the Trust's meeting on Monday had been presented with the Special Investigation Team's (SIT) preliminary report, which has now been made public. As the report had earlier remained confidential, he had refrained from commenting. Champat Rai said he would respond with facts to all the allegations and what he described as a smear campaign only after the SIT completes its final investigation. He expressed confidence that the truth would emerge once the final report is released. In the letter, he also wrote that he was deputed to Ayodhya by his organisation in 1991. Describing his nearly 45-year public life as an "open book", he said he believed that truth would ultimately prevail. He concluded by saying that he respects the truth and would wait for the final investigation report before making any further statement. Champat Rai resigned as the Trust's General Secretary on 26 June, and his resignation was accepted during the Trust meeting on 6 July. He is currently in Ayodhya. Govind Dev Giri says Champat Rai had no moral involvement Speaking on Tuesday, Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust Treasurer Swami Govind Dev Giri Ji Maharaj said that when he described Champat Rai as "innocent", he meant there could be no moral or personal involvement on his part in the alleged wrongdoing. However, he added that Champat Rai had failed to exercise due caution. "He appointed a man with a criminal background as his driver. The driver had access to the keys and controlled everything. It was the driver who carried out all this. I suspect he had links with outsiders. This happened because there was no Chief Executive Officer (CEO). We will now appoint a CEO," he said. Meanwhile, the Trust's newly appointed General Secretary, Krishna Mohan Das, formally assumed charge on Tuesday. Three accused remanded to police custody for one day The Faizabad Anti-Corruption Court granted the police one day's remand of three accused, Karunesh Pandey, Anukalp Mishra and Lavkush. The police had sought seven days' custody. The three accused will now be brought from jail on Wednesday morning for questioning.

stories.title: UP to issue passport-style driving licences:Automatic test, police verification mandatory; cameras, sensors to decide pass or fail
stories.summary: Driving licences in Uttar Pradesh will soon be issued on the pattern of passports, with police verification becoming part of the process. After online slot booking, applicants will have to appear for an interview with officials, followed by a driving test. The Transport Department is expected to issue new rules soon. The government aims to ensure that licences are issued only to people who can drive properly and are aware of traffic rules. Digital token system will also be implemented in RTOs Like passport service centres, Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) will also introduce a digital token system. Applicants will receive tokens according to their scheduled time slots. Only after their number appears on the display screen will they be allowed to enter counters for biometric verification, photographs and other procedures. The move is expected to reduce overcrowding at RTO offices and limit the role of middlemen. Police verification before issuing driving licences Police verification will be carried out before issuing driving licences. At present, such verification is conducted only before issuing passports. It may include checking the applicant’s address and criminal record. The Transport Department is currently examining how the system can be implemented under existing laws. According to the department’s proposal, police verification will not be mandatory for everyone. It will apply in two situations: Cameras, sensors and computers will test your driving Till now, driving tests at RTOs were conducted manually. Under the new system, tests will be held at recognised high-tech driving training centres, where sensors, cameras and computer-based systems will assess driving skills. This will make it difficult to obtain licences through recommendations or bribery. Major RTOs in Uttar Pradesh, including Lucknow, Kanpur, Noida and Ghaziabad, are being connected with automated driving test tracks. These tracks have three types of tests: Chances of failing up to 40%, application cancelled if failed 3 times If the vehicle’s tyre touches the yellow line on the track or hits sensor-based poles during the test, the computer system will immediately mark the applicant as ‘FAIL’ without any human intervention. The failure rate in these tests is more than 40%. The automated driving test system has strict rules. If an applicant fails for the first time, they cannot appear for the test the next day. They will have to book a new slot after at least seven days. If an applicant fails three consecutive times, the application will be cancelled. The person will not be able to apply again for six months and will have to restart the entire process. Live photo and biometric verification before test When applicants reach the RTO, their live photograph and biometric details will be recorded and matched with Aadhaar data. The same person will then have to appear for the driving test. Biometric verification will also be done before the test, making it impossible for someone else to take the test on the applicant’s behalf. The entire process will be uploaded immediately on the government’s Sarathi portal, helping curb middlemen, recommendations and fake licences. 28-day training certificate holders to get exemption The government has also provided some relief. Applicants who complete 28 days of training at a government-recognised driving training centre and receive Form-5 will not need to appear separately for an RTO or automated track driving test. They will be directly issued a permanent driving licence. This exemption will only apply to certified Driving Training Centres (DTCs) recognised by the Transport Department. Changes being made to prevent road accidents According to the Transport Department, Uttar Pradesh currently has around 2.99 crore active driving licences. Lucknow RTO alone has issued the highest number of licences in the state, with around 13.66 lakh licences. Government inspections and road safety audits have found that many road users are unaware of traffic rules. To address this issue, the rules for issuing driving licences are being changed. stories.title: Man murdered two months after selling ₹2 crore plot:Bodies found in Jhajjar; faces beaten, attempt made to burn them
stories.summary: Several revelations have now emerged regarding the semi-naked dead body on Gurugram-Jhajjar Road. Family members say that the deceased Kamil had sold a plot worth about 2 crore rupees just 2 months ago. On July 4, he had gone to Neemrana in Rajasthan with his associate Irshad in a black Scorpio. Kamil used to run a PG here, while Irshad worked as a clerk in the same PG. On Monday morning, both their bodies were found near Sehwag International School in Jhajjar. Both bodies were lying on top of each other. One had a serious head injury. Near their bodies, a blue drum containing petroleum substance, a pipe, an iron sheet, and truck keys were found. Now Jhajjar police believe both were murdered over the 2 crore transaction. After that, their bodies were brought in a truck and dumped by the roadside. The accused were preparing to burn both bodies here, but as soon as they got wind of someone coming there, the accused fled from the spot. Police are also now investigating the transaction. Full sequence of the double murder case He said that they spoke on the phone on Sunday and everything seemed normal, but on Monday they received information about their murder. Irshad had worked with Kamal for 20 years Irshad’s brother Haqiqat said that Irshad had been living and working with Kamal for nearly 20 years. "Both worked together. Their relationship had become like that of a family. Irshad worked as a manager at the PG. Many times, they even visited home together," he said. After selling the plot, Kamal had also started working as a property dealer. Post-mortem of bodies will be done today Kamal is survived by three sons and three daughters. Two of his sons are married. Irshad’s family includes three daughters. The postmortem of both bodies will be conducted today. The report is expected to reveal the time of death, the method used in the crime and other important details. SHO said - Police investigating from every angle SHO Paramjeet said that police are investigating all possible angles, including financial transactions, property dealings and old rivalries. The investigation team is trying to identify the accused through technical evidence. Police said the complete case would be revealed soon.

stories.title: Newborn falls on floor after delivery, dies:Chaos at Lucknow government hospital; father alleges negligence, demands action
stories.summary: A newborn baby died after allegedly falling on the floor during delivery at a government hospital in Lucknow. The family created a ruckus, alleging that when they brought the woman to the hospital, they were told to wait until labour pain increased before conducting a normal delivery. The baby's father said it was his wife's first pregnancy and that she had delivered a baby boy. The incident took place at Lok Bandhu Raj Narayan Combined Hospital on Kanpur Road. Shubham, a resident of Sita Vihar Colony in Ashiyana, brought his pregnant wife to the hospital on Sunday evening after she developed labour pain. Shubham alleged that a cleaning staff member at the hospital demanded ₹500 for conducting the delivery. He claimed she told him, "The doctors give me ₹50, you give me ₹500 and I will get the delivery done." Read the child's father's allegation- Father alleges doctors delayed delivery, refused C-section The baby's father, Shubham Pal, said his wife was admitted around 4 pm on Sunday after she developed labour pain. "After admission, they kept waiting for the labour pain to increase and said that normal delivery would be done only after that. At the time of admission, doctors had said that if required, a C-section could also be performed," he said. Shubham alleged that even after five hours, normal delivery could not happen and his wife had become exhausted. "I requested them to perform a C-section, but the doctors said they did not have the facility for it. I then went to the director and told him the same. He said that the hospital had complete arrangements for a C-section," Shubham claimed. He said he submitted a written complaint to the hospital director, who assured him that the matter would be investigated and justice would be provided. Shubham also questioned whether doctors or interns were on duty during the incident, claiming that even the director did not have information about who was assigned duty at that time. My mother was pushed out of the labor room Shubham said he admitted his wife to the hospital at 4 pm on Sunday. Later, labour pain started again at around 4 am, after which she was taken to the labour room for an attempt at normal delivery until 8:30 am. "During this time, my mother was also inside the delivery room. The staff pushed her out. There was no doctor present there at that time," he alleged. He repeated that a cleaning worker told him that doctors paid her ₹50 and asked him to give ₹500 so she could get the delivery done. Baby fell on floor during delivery, family alleges doctors did not respond Shubham said his wife Kirti's condition kept worsening. Eventually, the delivery took place, but during the process, the baby fell on the floor and suffered a head injury. He alleged that despite the incident, no doctor came to check the patient in the ward. "The family created a commotion, after which some nursing staff and employees arrived," he said. Family members demanded CCTV footage The family alleged that doctors wanted to complete paperwork and send the deceased newborn home. Shubham refused to accept the body and demanded a postmortem. After receiving information about the protest, local police reached the hospital. Following the family's demand, police sent the newborn's body for postmortem. Shubham also demanded CCTV footage from the hospital administration to investigate what happened during the delivery. Hospital forms three-member committee Lok Bandhu Hospital Director Dr Rajesh Kumar said a three-member committee has been formed to investigate the matter. The committee will examine the family's written complaint and allegations. Statements of doctors, nursing staff and other employees present on duty will also be recorded. Medical records, duty rosters and the entire delivery process will be reviewed. If negligence is confirmed at any level, action will be taken against the concerned doctors and staff according to rules. The committee has been directed to submit its report soon. Deputy CM took cognizance, demanded report within 24 hours Deputy Chief Minister and Health Minister Brajesh Pathak has taken cognisance of the newborn's death. He has sought a report within 24 hours and directed the Director General of Medical and Health to investigate the matter. He said strict action should be taken against those found guilty and that negligence in healthcare services would not be tolerated. The government’s priority is to provide better treatment facilities to pregnant women and new mothers, he said.

stories.title: Ram Mandir theft accused Avinash’s lavish spending exposed:Spent ₹6 lakh on brother’s wedding, gifted girlfriend an iPhone
stories.summary: The investigation into the Ram Mandir donation theft case has brought several new revelations during the questioning of accused Avinash Shukla. According to sources, Avinash admitted that a major portion of the allegedly stolen donation money was spent on his family, friends and personal expenses. He reportedly spent around ₹19 lakh on relatives and acquaintances. Sources said Avinash spent nearly ₹6 lakh on his brother’s wedding, gave around ₹5-6 lakh to another brother, gifted an iPhone to his girlfriend and transferred ₹2.5 lakh to her online. Investigating agencies are now examining these transactions, bank accounts and properties linked to the accused. Money transferred to others may be recovered During the investigation, it also emerged that Avinash bought a Brezza car by paying around ₹3.5 lakh as a down payment on loan. Police have already recovered the vehicle. Investigators have found that Avinash allegedly gave smaller amounts of money to several other people as well. Police questioned both of Avinash’s brothers and seized some documents. The land purchased in the name of his brother Abhishek Shukla in 2024 and related bank accounts are also being examined. Legal proceedings have been initiated to recover the money transferred to different people. Police recover ₹20.39 lakh cash, 1,121 dollars and jewellery So far, police have recovered ₹20.39 lakh in cash, 1,121 US dollars (around ₹1.06 lakh), gold and silver jewellery and other valuables from Avinash Shukla. On June 28, police raided Avinash’s yoga centre in Ayodhya. During the search, they recovered a box marked ‘Ramrajya Kosh’. A Paytm QR code was also attached to it. Police also found several documents and books related to the Ram Mandir from the premises. According to sources, Avinash’s brother Abhishek had once questioned accused Anukalp Mishra about the source of money. Anukalp allegedly avoided answering and warned him against asking further questions. Cash was recovered from the house on June 5 During the search of Avinash Shukla’s yoga centre in Ayodhya, police recovered several documents and books linked to the Ram Mandir. Earlier, on June 5, security personnel of the Trust had raided Avinash’s house. It was claimed that cash was recovered from the house. The recovered money was reportedly packed in bags and taken away by security personnel. Police are now examining the documents and other items recovered from Avinash to connect the missing links in the case. Yoga Center Staff Said - Avinash Came One and a Half Years Ago Yoga centre employees say Avinash joined around 1.5 years ago Shiv Sundar Lal, an employee at the yoga centre, said Avinash Shukla and his brother Abhishek had been associated with the centre for a long time. He said Abhishek had been staying there for around 10 years as he was associated with the centre since the time of the revered Guruji and used to serve him. Avinash also started living there with his brother around one-and-a-half years ago. “When we came to know that Avinash got a job at Ram Mandir, we were very happy. He used to leave for work on time every morning and return in the evening. His behaviour was always calm, polite and normal. He never gave any indication that could raise suspicion,” he said. However, after police arrived on June 5 and reports emerged about the recovery of cash bags during the search, everyone at the centre was shocked. “We never imagined that he could be involved in any illegal activity. As soon as the matter came out and reached the media, we took a strict stand,” he said. He added that keeping the reputation of the institution in mind, the family was asked on June 6 to make arrangements to leave the centre. “Whoever is guilty should get the strictest punishment under the law. We are fully cooperating with the investigation,” he said. Yoga trainer says Avinash was asked to leave after video surfaced Yoga instructor Seema Tiwari of Shyam Sadhnalaya Yoga Centre said Avinash had been living there for around one-and-a-half years, while his brother Abhishek had been there for about 10 years. She said the centre was run by Dr Chaitanya, who had educated and supported many young people and provided them shelter. Abhishek was also among them. She said Abhishek brought Avinash to the centre after informing them that he had got a job at the Ram Mandir. “When we heard that his name had appeared in the embezzlement case, we were shocked. Police came here on June 5. When the video went viral and we came to know that some bags were recovered from here, we spoke to Abhishek the next day,” she said. She added that they told the brothers, “Please leave from here. The centre’s reputation is being affected.” Avinash and Abhishek left the centre on June 6. Villagers claim Avinash built a new house Avinash Shukla, accused in the Ram Mandir donation theft case, is a resident of Babupur Nariyawa village under Maheshganj police station area. His father Ram Sajeevan Shukla is a farmer. Avinash is the second among five brothers. His elder brother Abhishek is a teacher in Ayodhya. Villagers told Dainik Bhaskar that Avinash’s ancestral house is a kutcha house where his parents live. However, a few months ago, Avinash and Abhishek built a new pucca house. Whenever the two brothers visited the village, they stayed in the newly built house. Avinash had been living in Ayodhya for one and a half years Avinash Shukla, accused in the Ram Mandir donation theft case, had been living in Ayodhya for the past one-and-a-half years. He was running a yoga centre and had also been working inside the Ram Mandir complex for the same period. His monthly salary was around ₹15,000. According to neighbours, Avinash and his brother used to sleep on the floor on blankets.

stories.title: SIT finds 70 theft incidents in Ram Mandir case:6 accused named after CCTV probe; staff seen hiding cash in pockets
stories.summary: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the alleged theft of donations at Ayodhya’s Ram Mandir submitted its preliminary report on Monday night around 9 pm, shortly after the Trust meeting where Champat Rai and Anil Mishra’s resignations were accepted. According to the report, nearly 70 suspicious incidents were captured on CCTV cameras between April 27 and June 5. The footage allegedly shows the eight accused, who are currently in police custody, hiding bundles of currency notes inside their pockets and shoes. The SIT has also levelled serious allegations against Dr Anil Mishra, saying he was responsible for loopholes in the existing search and security system that allowed the alleged theft to take place. The report states that Champat Rai’s driver Tinnu kept the keys of the counting room with him without any official order. It also alleges that he had recommended his nephew Manish Yadav for work related to counting donations. The Uttar Pradesh government had formed the SIT to investigate the alleged theft of Ram Mandir offerings. The team submitted its initial report to the government on June 23. The SIT includes Lucknow Divisional Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant, Lucknow Range IG Kiran S and Special Secretary in the UP Finance Department Neel Ratan. Key Points of SIT's Primary Report Anil Mishra held responsible for flaws in donation counting process The SIT said the entire process of counting donations was found to have several loopholes. According to the report, Dr Anil Mishra was overseeing financial matters and cash collection management. He also played an important role in preparing the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) and coordination points with the bank. The SIT said he was responsible for ensuring proper monitoring of the process. Security system had loopholes despite information about missing searches The SIT stated that information about employees not being searched properly had already reached Anil Mishra through internal channels. However, despite this, no effective written order or instruction was issued to correct the problem. The report said the previously established search system was also weakened due to negligence attributed to Anil Mishra. No attendance system or paperwork increased chances of theft The SIT found that several important security measures were not properly implemented. These included: According to the report, weak monitoring encouraged accused employees and they continued stealing money from Ram Lalla’s treasury. Employees hid cash bundles in clothes, pockets, shoes and socks The SIT said CCTV footage recorded between April 27 and June 5, 2026 showed some employees working in the donation counting room repeatedly hiding currency bundles and loose notes inside their clothes, pockets, shoes and socks. The report said the absence of checking at entry and exit points made it possible to take cash outside the premises. Employees filled pockets with notes, alerted each other through signals The SIT said the incidents were not isolated but part of a repeated organised activity. The investigation recorded around 70 such incidents. Some employees were also seen using gestures to alert each other during the alleged thefts. Report reveals- 6 accused directly involved in theft According to the SIT, Avinash Shukla, Anukalp Mishra, Lavkush Mishra, Manish Kumar Yadav, Karunesh Pandey and Ramashankar Mishra appeared to be directly involved at the preliminary stage. The SIT said CCTV footage, recovery of stolen money and bank account investigations provided sufficient evidence against them. The report recommended registering cases against them under sections related to theft, criminal breach of trust, criminal misappropriation, possession of stolen property and conspiracy. Based on the SIT report, trustee Krishna Mohan filed the case. Later, the accused were arrested and are currently in jail. Avinash had ₹20.39 lakh cash, 1,121 dollars and car recovered According to police sources, accused Avinash has allegedly confessed that he spent around ₹19 lakh on friends and family members. He reportedly spent nearly ₹6 lakh on one brother’s wedding celebrations and gave ₹5 lakh to another brother. He also purchased a car worth ₹3.5 lakh. The investigation found that Avinash transferred around ₹2.5 lakh to a friend and also gifted him an expensive mobile phone. Officials are also investigating land purchased in 2024 in the name of his brother Abhishek Shukla. Legal action has been initiated to recover the money. So far, ₹20.39 lakh in cash, 1,121 US dollars, gold jewellery and silver ornaments have been recovered from Shukla. Tinnu had donation box keys without written order The SIT report also mentioned that Ramashankar Yadav alias Tinnu had control over the keys of temple donation boxes and related access arrangements without any formal written order. According to the report, on Tinnu’s recommendation, Manish Kumar Yadav was appointed for counting work, who was later found allegedly involved in theft. The SIT described this as a serious security lapse. Employees earning ₹20,000 had lakhs in accounts, financial transactions under scanner The SIT also examined bank accounts of the accused employees and their family members. According to the report, the employees earned around ₹20,000 per month, but their accounts showed large cash deposits, fixed deposits and other transactions that did not match their declared income. The SIT suspects that the stolen money may have been diverted into bank accounts and properties. A detailed investigation has been recommended into these transactions. 2 pictures related to the Ram Temple Trust meeting SIT says investigation still underway, final report will include more findings The SIT clarified that the current report is only a preliminary investigation. The team said investigation is still underway into security failures, responsibility of officials, system weaknesses, possible involvement of other people and measures needed to prevent such incidents in the future. Detailed findings and recommendations will be submitted to the government in the final report.
