stories.title: 6-murder accused Asif Ali shot dead in STF encounter:2 bullets hit chest after firing at team, wanted in Jaunpur double murder
stories.summary: UP STF shot dead gangster Asif Ali (40) in an encounter in Ambedkar Nagar at around 4 am on Tuesday. STF officials said Asif opened fire after being surrounded, prompting retaliatory firing in which he was hit by two bullets in the chest. The encounter took place near Jagdishpur village, around 25 km from the district headquarters. Asif was the head of the Chhaimar gang and was wanted in six murders, including the killings of a husband and wife. Police said the gang used a distinctive modus operandi, carrying out robberies at night while dressed in underwear and vests. Members would enter homes, hold families hostage, loot valuables and kill victims before fleeing. Asif would then allegedly change his identity and hide in other districts and states. Investigators say almost all crimes linked to him followed the same pattern. According to Rajkumar Mishra, Additional SP of the Noida STF unit, Asif was wanted in a 2014 Jaunpur robbery in which two women were killed. Three others were also attacked but survived. Jaunpur Police had announced a reward of ₹1 lakh on him. He was facing 20 criminal cases across Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Haryana. STF surrounded him, he opened fire; killed in retaliatory firing According to the UP STF, they had received information from an informer that Asif was hiding in Ambedkar Nagar and was planning another crime. After this, the team surrounded him. Seeing himself trapped, Asif tried to escape by turning his bike. When the STF team chased him, he opened fire. A constable suffered a bullet injury in his right hand. Following this, the STF team retaliated. Two bullets hit Asif in the chest, after which he fell to the ground. The team rushed him to the district hospital, where he died during treatment. STF recovered a pistol, a country-made 12-bore firearm and a motorcycle from him. Chhaimar gang leader wanted in six murders Police describe the Chhaimar gang as a notorious criminal network operating mainly at night and involved in theft, robbery and dacoity. Members frequently shifted locations across Uttar Pradesh and other states to evade arrest, often using fake identities. The gang reportedly functioned in a manner similar to the Kachha-Baniyan and Bawaria gangs and followed a strict hierarchy. According to police, only a member involved in at least six murders could become the gang leader, which is why it came to be known as the Chhaimar gang. The most ruthless criminal within the group was given the title of "Rajkumar". Women were also part of the network and allegedly conducted reconnaissance during the day by posing as beggars or ragpickers. At night, gang members would hide near targeted homes before striking. Police said gang members worshipped Goddess Kali and offered liquor before carrying out robberies. They would then enter houses wearing only underwear and vests. If victims resisted, they were allegedly killed using sharp-edged weapons, as firearms could attract attention due to the sound of gunshots. ₹1 lakh reward announced after Jaunpur double murder Noida STF unit Additional SP Rajkumar Mishra said Ali and his gang had carried out a robbery in Jaunpur where two women were killed. Three other people were also attacked but survived. Following the incident, Jaunpur Police announced a reward of ₹1 lakh on information leading to Ali’s arrest. Police said 20 cases were registered against him across Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Haryana. Asif Ali’s major criminal cases On October 19, 2013, Asif and 10 gang members allegedly entered a house in Sultanpur, carried out a robbery and held the family hostage. One person was killed during the incident. In 2014, Asif and his associates allegedly entered a house in Shahganj, Jaunpur, held the family hostage and looted jewellery and cash worth lakhs of rupees. They also allegedly attacked five family members with sharp weapons. Two women, Swati and Suman, later died during treatment. On August 15, 2015, Asif and his gang members allegedly committed a robbery in Kaushambi, held the family hostage and killed a husband and wife. On August 19, 2015, Asif and 10 associates allegedly entered the house of Mahavir Singh in the Muzaffarnagar area and carried out a robbery. Mahavir’s daughter-in-law was allegedly attacked with a sharp weapon. The same night, the gang allegedly targeted five more houses. On January 13, 2021, Asif allegedly entered a house in Rasulabad, Kanpur Dehat, and killed a man named Tasim. Chhaimar gang: Daytime surveillance, night-time robberies The Chhaimar gang is considered one of Uttar Pradesh’s notorious criminal groups, known for carrying out thefts, robberies and dacoities at night. Police said the gang frequently changed locations across Uttar Pradesh and other states after crimes to avoid detection. The gang reportedly operates like the Kachha-Baniyan and Bawariya gangs, with strict internal rules. According to police, a person becomes the gang leader only after committing at least six murders, which is why the group is known as the “Chhaimar gang”. Police said members who commit more violent crimes gain higher status within the gang, with the most ruthless criminal being given the title of “Rajkumar”. Women are also allegedly part of the gang and conduct daytime surveillance by posing as beggars or waste collectors. Before targeting a house, gang members allegedly hide nearby at night. Police said they traditionally enter homes wearing vests and shorts and avoid using firearms during robberies to prevent attracting attention. If victims resist, they allegedly attack them with sharp weapons.

stories.title: Monsoon intensifies with heavy rain in UP:Highways waterlogged; roads turn into rivers in Mathura, cars swept away in Shamli
stories.summary: The monsoon has gathered pace across Uttar Pradesh. Since Tuesday morning, rainfall has been reported in around 50 cities, including Lucknow, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Chandauli and Moradabad. In Shamli, heavy rain turned roads into fast-flowing streams. Cars and motorcycles were seen being swept along by the water, while children were spotted swimming on flooded streets as if they were in a swimming pool. Flooding disrupts normal life in several districts In Vrindavan, Mathura, roads resembled rivers due to heavy rainfall. In Amroha, just one hour of rain caused waterlogging on the Delhi–Lucknow Highway. In Varanasi, rainwater cascaded down stairways like waterfalls. Strong winds forced boat operators to suspend services. In Hapur, markets were inundated, with floodwater entering shops. Traders were seen sitting on stools to keep themselves above the rising water. Rain alert issued for all 75 districts The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh on Tuesday, with heavy rainfall forecast in eight districts. Near the Maa Shakambhari Devi Temple in Saharanpur, the Shakambhari River witnessed a sudden surge in water levels, triggering panic among visitors. Police used loudspeakers to warn people to leave the riverbank immediately as water levels were rising rapidly. Heavy rain also affected rail services on Monday Rainfall was recorded in 48 cities across the state on Monday. At Varanasi railway station, rainwater began leaking through the roof onto Platform No. 8, with water pouring through a ceiling fan like a waterfall. During the past 24 hours, Auraiya recorded the highest rainfall in the state at 35.9 mm, which is 379% above its normal rainfall of 7.5 mm. See photos of rain- Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said a low-pressure area had formed over the north-west Bay of Bengal. It crossed the northern Odisha coast and is now centred over southern Jharkhand and northern Chhattisgarh. He said the system has significantly strengthened the monsoon across Uttar Pradesh, and heavy rainfall is likely at several places across the state.

stories.title: Ram Mandir trust members opposed Champat Rai's resignation:Accepted due to Trust constitution's rules; Gopal Rao told to leave premises
stories.summary: Place: Ram Mandir complex, Yatri Suvidha Kendra Time: 2:45 pm, July 6, 2026 The atmosphere inside the Ram Mandir complex turned tense on July 6 as the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust held a crucial meeting after the controversy over alleged theft of temple offerings. As the trust members gathered for the meeting, Treasurer Govind Dev Giri arrived at the Yatri Suvidha Kendra. The moment he stepped out of his vehicle, he spotted invited trust member Gopal Rao standing outside the facility. Giri appeared upset and told him, "Move away… leave from here. If you stay here, Nritya Gopal Das will not come." After hearing this, Gopal Rao paused for a moment, held his mobile phone in his hand and slowly walked towards the control room inside the Ram Mandir complex. He stayed there and did not come outside. Soon after this exchange, Govind Dev Giri entered the room where the important trust meeting was scheduled. Within around 15 minutes, all members reached the venue. Shortly afterwards, Trust President Mahant Nritya Gopal Das arrived in a wheelchair along with his disciple Kamal Nayan Das. Govind Dev Giri placed resignation papers before members and said: "Accept it or not..." The meeting room had sofas covered mostly with saffron cloth. Trustees including Dinendra Das, Swami Parmanand and Swami Vasudevanand were present. A laptop was placed on a table through which some trustees joined the meeting online. At exactly 3 pm, Govind Dev Giri began discussions on the agenda. He placed some documents on the table and said: “Ram devotees' faith has been hurt. Something unimaginable has happened. This has caused deep pain to Trust General Secretary Champat Rai. Until justice is properly delivered and the guilty are caught, it does not seem appropriate for him to continue in the Trust. He has submitted his resignation. Whether it should be accepted or not is not in our hands.” After making this statement, Giri stopped speaking. Silence prevailed in the room for some time. Later, most members expressed the view that Champat Rai's resignation should not be accepted. K. Parasaran read Trust rules, said resignation was automatically accepted Senior advocate K. Parasaran joined the meeting online. He explained that according to the Trust's constitution, a resignation submitted by a member is considered automatically accepted. He then displayed pages of the Trust constitution on the screen and read out the relevant clauses. This clarified to the members that they did not have the option to either accept or reject the resignation. According to the rules, the resignation had already come into effect once submitted. Following this, President Mahant Nritya Gopal Das, Dinendra Das and other trustees agreed to accept Champat Rai's resignation. Trustees express anger over Dr Anil Mishra’s role, call it negligence After Champat Rai's resignation, the meeting moved towards discussing the resignation of trustee Dr Anil Mishra. Most trustees appeared unhappy with him because the responsibility of the counting room was under his supervision. Members acknowledged that there had been clear negligence. The discussion then turned towards invited member Gopal Rao. Trustees said he was inducted into the Trust in 2020 but had not contributed towards improving temple arrangements. Members agreed to remove him from the Trust. Krishna Mohan’s name gets approval for general secretary post The trustees then discussed how the temple administration would function going forward. It was decided that Krishna Mohan would be appointed as the new general secretary to manage temple affairs. Most members agreed on his name. The trustees also agreed to appoint a Chief Executive Officer (CEO) in the future. Three names were shortlisted for setting the selection criteria: These three members will prepare the standards and present them before trustees during the July 22 meeting. Trust admitted, ‘People should have been told the right things’ During the meeting, trustees also discussed the issue of devotees claiming their donated items. Members admitted that the Trust had never clearly communicated the status of such offerings, leading to confusion among people. Treasurer Govind Dev Giri then presented a register containing details of 2,800 items. It was decided that the complete information should be made public. Champat arrived, but he was not included in the meeting Champat Rai also reached the Yatri Suvidha Kendra at the scheduled time. However, after some discussion with Trust members, he remained near the complex and did not enter the meeting room. Meanwhile, trustee Dr Anil Mishra did not attend the meeting.

stories.title: 'Honeymoon plan was a trap,' family alleges:Bihar woman dies in Lucknow, husband accused of planned murder over dowry disputes
stories.summary: "I can say with complete conviction that my sister-in-law was not the kind of person who would take her own life. She was a B.Sc graduate, academically bright and mentally strong. She faced every challenge head-on. She was murdered in a planned manner, and more than one person is involved. The accused husband first called her to Lucknow on the pretext of taking her to Kashmir for a honeymoon. Two days before the incident, he shifted to a new flat. After that, she was killed. The flat he moved into had no neighbouring tenants nearby, which made it easier to execute the crime without any disturbance. Our family wants justice. Police should arrest not only accused Kamalakant but also his family members." These are the allegations made by the victim's brother-in-law, Ravishankar Dubey. A 24-year-old woman from Bihar's Buxar district died under suspicious circumstances in Lucknow on 4 July, barely four months after her marriage. Her family has accused her husband and in-laws of dowry murder. The deceased has been identified as Sonali, daughter of Virendra Ojha, a resident of Khadhatand village in Buxar district. The accused, Kamalakant Mishra (28), belongs to Pinjarouli village under Sandesh police station limits in Bhojpur district. On the evening of 6 July 2026, Lucknow Police arrested Kamalakant after questioning him. Police are currently awaiting the post-mortem report. A team visited Sonali's parental home, located around 50 kilometres from the Buxar district headquarters, and spoke to her father, brother and brother-in-law. Now read the complete news in a sequential manner... First, see the pictures related to the incident... Son-in-law killed daughter after arranged marriage Family alleges husband photographed body before taking her to hospital According to the victim's family, photographs submitted to police show that instead of rushing Sonali to hospital, her husband first took pictures with her body. The family also produced WhatsApp chats in which Kamalakant allegedly abused Sonali, called her "illiterate" and used derogatory language. Father alleges repeated demand for car despite ₹15 lakh dowry Sonali's father, Virendra Jain, said his daughter married Kamalakant Mishra in an arranged marriage on February 26, 2026. He alleged that the family gave ₹15 lakh in cash, around 250 grams of gold jewellery and furniture worth nearly ₹2.5 lakh as dowry. "Despite this, Kamalakant and his family repeatedly demanded a car after the marriage," he said. According to him, for nearly two months after the wedding, Kamalakant neither took Sonali with him nor allowed her to go to her matrimonial home. The family allegedly insisted that she would be accepted only after a car was provided. After persuasion, they reportedly agreed to take Sonali but told her family that a car should be gifted later. Virendra alleged that Kamalakant's family wanted Sonali to be sent to her marital home with a car during the gauna ceremony. However, due to financial constraints, Sonali was sent to her in-laws in April 2026 with her brother Abhishek. After moving there, Sonali allegedly told her siblings that she was being abused, beaten and harassed for dowry. Her father claimed she sent screenshots of abusive messages from her husband to her brother. In the chats, Kamalakant allegedly threatened her, used obscene language, mocked her appearance and called her an "illiterate villager". He alleged that the accused had already planned the murder. See pictures of the wedding... Brother says Sonali spoke of harassment and later Kashmir honeymoon plan Sonali's brother Abhishek said she stayed at her parental home for two months after marriage and moved to her in-laws' house only in April 2026. He alleged that Sonali regularly informed the family that her in-laws, including her parents-in-law, sister-in-law, elder brother-in-law and his wife, verbally abused and physically assaulted her. When the family learned about the alleged harassment, they contacted her in-laws and told them that they had already spent everything they had and could not provide any additional dowry. Abhishek said Sonali spoke to him on June 20 and said Kamalakant was taking her to Kashmir for a honeymoon. "She told me that Kamalakant had started behaving lovingly and that everything between them was improving. She said he would take her from Ara to Lucknow by the end of the week and assured us that things would become normal," he said. The family believed the relationship was improving and hoped to discuss the car issue later. However, on June 26, Sonali reportedly called her brother in tears and said Kamalakant had abused her, called her uneducated and that she no longer wanted to go with him. The family assumed it was a temporary marital dispute and advised her to talk things through. On June 28, Sonali travelled from Ara to Lucknow. Couple was scheduled to leave for Kashmir on July 5 The couple was supposed to fly to Jammu and Kashmir on July 5. However, on the afternoon of July 4, Kamalakant called Abhishek and informed him that Sonali had died by suicide. He also allegedly sent a WhatsApp photograph showing Sonali lying on the floor while he was posing beside her body. The family maintains that Sonali was murdered and that an attempt was made to portray it as suicide. They claimed that when they saw the body, they noticed injury marks not only around her neck but also on both hands and legs. According to the family, these injuries suggest that Sonali's hands and legs may have been restrained before she was killed. They have demanded a fair investigation into the role of Kamalakant and other family members. Abhishek said the family possesses WhatsApp chats and other evidence showing prolonged harassment and threats against Sonali, which they plan to submit before investigators and the court. They have appealed to the government and administration to ensure a scientific, transparent and impartial probe. Injury marks found on neck, legs and hands Ravishankar Dubey, Sonali's brother-in-law, said he lives in Ara and works with the railways in Madhya Pradesh. He said he reached home immediately after receiving information about the incident. "I have known Sonali for eight years. Based on her personality and determination, I can say with certainty that she was not someone who would commit suicide. She was mentally strong and faced every challenge fearlessly," he said. He alleged that the death appeared to be a carefully planned murder disguised as suicide. Dubey said the injury marks on Sonali's neck, hands and legs raise suspicion that more than one person may have been involved. At the same time, he acknowledged that the truth would emerge only after the post-mortem report, forensic examination and an impartial police investigation. He urged authorities not to close the case by treating it as a suicide and instead investigate every angle scientifically. Family questions lack of public support Dubey also expressed disappointment over what he described as a lack of public attention. He referred to the recent Bharat Tiwari murder case, saying society, media and public representatives had raised their voices strongly in that matter. "What happened to him was wrong and the guilty should be punished. But similar sensitivity is not being shown in our daughter's case," he said. He alleged that people still try to murder women and disguise such crimes as suicides. The family claimed that no social organisation, community representative or public figure had visited them to understand what happened. They further alleged attempts were made to suppress the case and claimed police were initially reluctant to conduct a post-mortem examination. According to them, the autopsy was carried out only after persistent pressure from family members. Dubey appealed to society, the media and authorities to treat the matter seriously, saying it was not just about one family's daughter but about justice and safety for all women. He said the family would cooperate fully with investigators and provide every piece of evidence available with them. "Our only demand is a fair and thorough investigation so that the truth comes out and whoever is responsible receives the strictest punishment under the law," he said. Husband claims dispute began after flight tickets were cancelled During questioning, Kamalakant told Lucknow Police that he and Sonali could not go on a honeymoon immediately after marriage because of his job commitments. He said they planned a trip to Kashmir a month ago and booked flight tickets. According to him, bad weather forced him to cancel the July 3 flight and book train tickets instead. He claimed Sonali became upset because she wanted to travel by air and that an argument followed despite his attempts to calm her down. Kamalakant said he left for work at around 10 am on July 4 as usual. At around noon, he called Sonali but received no response. He then contacted the landlord and asked him to check on her. According to his statement, the landlord found the door locked from inside. Kamalakant said he rushed home and found Sonali hanging from the ceiling when he opened the door. Following a complaint filed by Sonali's brother Abhishek, Indiranagar Police in Lucknow registered a case of dowry death and other related charges against six members of the husband's family, including Kamalakant, his mother Ramavati, father Shardanand, sister Girija Chaubey, elder brother Laxmikant and sister-in-law Lakshmi. Police have arrested Kamalakant and seized the mobile phones of the husband and wife. Investigators have recovered chats exchanged between the couple as well as conversations between Kamalakant and his sister Girija. According to police sources, the chats allegedly contain references to "teaching Sonali a lesson" and even discussions about taking her life.

stories.title: Shankaracharya's sexual exploitation case was 'conspiracy':Ashutosh Maharaj used threats to secure false statements, claims 'batuk'
stories.summary: At the Magh Mela in Prayagraj, chants from a tent marked the conclusion of a yajna ceremony. After the ritual ended, Shakambhari Peethadheeshwar Ashutosh Brahmachari allegedly called two batuks, placed his hand on their heads, gave them ₹6,000 each as dakshina, collected their Aadhaar cards for making dakshina cards and obtained their signatures on blank sheets of paper. According to an investigation by Dainik Bhaskar, it was from this point that an alleged conspiracy to implicate Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand in a sexual exploitation case began. The report claims Ashutosh later used those signed blank papers to prepare statements alleging sexual harassment. Bhaskar said it conducted a four-month investigation, during which a batuk, his father and uncle spoke on hidden camera about the alleged sequence of events. Why these two batuks were allegedly chosen The report traces the story back nearly a year. The two batuks had participated in yajnas held in two different cities of Uttar Pradesh and had reportedly received ₹60,000 each as dakshina. It was during this period that they came into contact with Ashutosh Maharaj. According to the investigation, four reasons were cited for allegedly choosing them as complainants in the Shankaracharya case: Batuk says he never knew or met the Shankaracharya Dainik Bhaskar reporters visited a village near Lucknow where one of the batuks lives with his family. They first spoke to the batuk. Reporter: Do you know Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand? Batuk: No, I do not know him. Reporter: Have you ever met him? Batuk: No. Reporter: Did you ever go to his ashram to study? Batuk: No, never. Reporter: Do you know what the case was about? Batuk: No, I did not know. I came to know later. Reporter: What did you come to know later? Batuk: That Ashutosh made us level false allegations. Reporter: What allegations? Batuk: Allegations of sexual misconduct. Reporter: Did anything like that ever happen to you? Batuk: No, never. Reporter: Never? Batuk: Never. Reporter: How did Ashutosh take you along with him? Batuk: We had gone there to perform a yajna. He had called us to Prayagraj saying some acquaintances had organised a programme and that two of us should come. I and another batuk went there. Ashutosh then told us that we had to give testimony for Lord Krishna. During the conversation, the batuk's uncle arrived and took the reporters towards the fields outside the village. Reporter: When did the batuk go to Ashutosh's ashram? Uncle: During Magh, in January. Reporter: How did he go? Who took him there? Uncle: A person named Devikishore (name changed), who is older than him. We can introduce you to him. He took him there. Earlier, they had earned ₹60,000 from yajnas. He called and said, come with us and you will earn good money. They got tempted. Reporter: Then what happened? Uncle: We do not know how they trapped him. They said it was a case related to Laddu Gopal. Ashutosh came home carrying large idols of Laddu Gopal and said a case was going on in which they had to testify. How was the boy supposed to know whether he was giving testimony for Laddu Gopal or for someone else? Reporter: How much money have you received so far? Batuk: ₹6,000. Reporter: Did he mention the name of any official? Batuk: No. Reporter: Did he say that if you gave your statement, you would get something in return? Batuk: He said we would live in Mathura. He asked us to testify for Lord Krishna. He said a temple-house would be arranged there and life would be comfortable. The reporters then spoke to the batuk's father, who broke his silence for the first time. Reporter: Do you know what happened? Father: We have nothing to do with this. If someone can safely take us and safely bring us back, then we will tell everyone the truth. This boy is my son, and he has been trapped. Batuk says he was taken away while appearing for an exam The reporters later spoke jointly to the batuk, his father and uncle. Reporter: Did you stay with Ashutosh? Batuk: Yes, we had gone for a yajna. Uncle: The Aadhaar cards given for preparing dakshina cards were later used for everything else. Reporter: The FIR says that you studied at Shankaracharya's place and that he sexually assaulted you and made you sleep beside him. Was anything like that true? Batuk: No, I never even went there. Uncle: If he never went there, how could he tell lies? We too have to answer before God one day. The child went to Prayagraj for the first time. He went because of money or temptation. Reporter: Did Ashutosh make you level allegations that something wrong had happened? Uncle: Yes. Reporter: Did he promise money or anything else? Father: He said there would be ₹21,000 as dakshina. Batuk: I was writing an examination at school. Ashutosh sent two boys outside the school. They forced me and my father onto a motorcycle. Reporter: Where did they take you? Batuk: To a hotel. Then an SUV came and we were taken to Lucknow. Uncle: They effectively kept him under control for four or five days. Father: I was with him. They took away our mobile phones. We were locked inside two or three rooms. We kept crying. There were policemen there too. We pleaded with them to let us go, otherwise we would kill ourselves. Only then were we sent back home in a private vehicle. Signatures allegedly taken in advance on blank papers According to the report, Ashutosh anticipated that the batuk or his family might back out later. To ensure that his alleged conspiracy did not weaken, he first got both batuks to sign blank papers in the name of preparing dakshina cards. He later allegedly wrote statements of sexual exploitation on those papers himself. Reporter: The FIR states that you had gone to Prayagraj during the Kumbh. Is that true? Batuk: No, I never went there. Reporter: Then how did allegations of sexual assault get written into the FIR? Batuk: Ashutosh submitted written statements on his own. Reporter: But the signatures are yours. Batuk: He had taken our signatures earlier in the name of preparing dakshina cards. He said he would make dakshina cards for us and asked us to sign. Reporter: Did you read the FIR? Batuk: No. What is the current status of this case? Police are still investigating the matter. So far, no chargesheet has been filed before the court, nor has police questioned Avimukteshwaranand. Shankaracharya's disciple Mukundanand Giri has approached the court claiming the case is false. The matter is scheduled for hearing on 28 July. After speaking to the batuk and his family members, Dainik Bhaskar also spoke to Ashutosh Maharaj.

stories.title: BJP woman leader slaps youth inside police outpost:Officer watches; threatens to 'Teach him a lesson'
stories.summary: A female BJP leader slapped a young man inside a police outpost in Sultanpur, warning him, Just wait and watch where I send you. I'll teach you such a lesson you'll forget your place. The incident took place in front of the sub-inspector at Shahganj outpost on 8 July at 10:30 am. After a video of the assault surfaced, police registered a case against the BJP leader on Thursday at 12:30 pm. See 2 pictures Read the full story Arun Kumar Kori, a resident of Paltu Ka Purwa (Adarsh Nagar, Ghosiana), has filed a complaint with the police. Arun stated that he has been working for several years at Sahara Trading Company, located in Murari Das Gali, owned by Harshit Barnwal. On 8 July, Arun reached the Shahganj intersection for his office work. Just then, Pooja Kasaudhan, the district treasurer of BJP Mahila Morcha, and her son Raunak arrived there on a bike. As soon as they saw Arun, both started abusing him using casteist slurs. They started saying - Quit working for Harshit Arun alleges that the mother-son duo pressured him, saying that people of his caste have lost their minds. 'How many times have we told you to quit working for Harshit Beniwal? But you people don't listen.' When Arun protested, Raunak and Pooja Kasaudhan assaulted him right in the middle of the intersection. Entered outpost to save his life, but was beaten there too According to Arun, to save his life, Arun ran and entered the premises of the nearby Shahganj police outpost. After this, Pooja Kasaudhan also came inside the outpost with her son. The video that has surfaced also shows Pooja Kasaudhan abusing Arun right in front of outpost in-charge Avinash Chandra. She started saying, I have been watching continuously, he is following me. He is coming behind me with a mobile phone to his ear. Meanwhile, Daroga and Pooja Kasaudhan's son, Raunak, started talking. Just then, Pooja Kasaudhan got up from her chair and went to Arun. She asked him for his mobile phone. Arun then said that he was talking to the Daroga about this matter. As soon as she heard this, Pooja slapped Arun. Threatened while leaving, said - you will be killed Arun alleges that as Pooja Kasaudhan was leaving, she threatened him, saying, Mend your ways in time, otherwise, the government and administration are mine. You will be killed, and no one will even ask about you. After this, when Pooja Kasaudhan left, Arun Kumar filed a complaint at Kotwali Nagar, pleading for a case to be registered. Today, a case has been registered against BJP leader Pooja Kasaudhan. Pooja Kasaudhan has been associated with BJP for 10 years Pooja Kasaudhan's house is near the Shahganj intersection. There is a police outpost near her house. Near the outpost, her husband, Sandeep Gupta, has a large grocery store. He is counted among the big grocery traders in the district. Pooja Kasaudhan has been associated with BJP for about 10 years. She had claimed the ticket for Chairman in the last municipal elections, but the party did not give her the ticket. Currently, she is associated with the party as the District Treasurer. CO City Raghavendra Singh said, There is an ongoing land dispute between the woman leader and Arun. A case has been registered against the woman leader based on Arun's complaint. This incident occurred in front of the outpost in-charge, and a departmental inquiry is being conducted regarding it. Action will also be taken against the sub-inspector after the investigation.

stories.title: UP-TET answer key sparks controversy over 4 questions:1.8 lakh candidates raise objections
stories.summary: A controversy has erupted over the answer key for the Uttar Pradesh Teacher Eligibility Test (UP-TET), with candidates and teacher organisations objecting to the answers for four questions released by the Examination Regulatory Authority (Commission). Candidates allege that some incorrect answers have been marked as correct. They say they have submitted evidence supporting the correct answers and have demanded that the Commission revise the answer key. According to the BTC Teachers' Association, around 17.70 lakh candidates (88.77%) appeared for the UP-TET held in two shifts on 2nd, 3rd, and 4th July at 955 centres across the state. The candidates included 1.86 lakh teachers who have not yet qualified TET and must clear the exam by 31 August, 2027. Main dispute over the answers to these 4 questions 1. Environment/Disaster Management: 'Disaster' was called 'Emergency' 2. Hindi (Junior Level - First Shift): Two correct options in one question 3. Hindi Idiom: 'Ek aankh se dekhna' was stated to mean 'andhadhundh karna' 4. Sanskrit (Primary Level - Second Shift): Wrong answer on 'Ushma Varna' Teachers' association said - Register objections by 14 July and secure marks Anil Yadav, President of the BTC Teachers' Association, and other expert colleagues have appealed to all affected candidates to register their objections with evidence on these questions on the online portal promptly. Objections can be registered until 14 July. So that the final answer key can be improved and the candidates' rightful marks can be ensured.

stories.title: 12-year-old beaten to death with cricket bat:Child killed over 'no ball' dispute; teenager detained
stories.summary: A 12-year-old boy was beaten to death with a cricket bat during a cricket match in Bhadohi on Wednesday evening after refusing to call a disputed delivery a no-ball. The incident occurred around 5 pm in Bhanipur village under Durgaganj police station, about 26 km from the district headquarters. The victim, identified as Aditya, was watching the match when players sought his opinion after the accused, who had been clean bowled, claimed the delivery was a no-ball to avoid being declared out. When Aditya said it was not a no-ball, the accused allegedly flew into a rage and repeatedly struck him on the head with a cricket bat. He was rushed to hospital but died during treatment at 8:28 pm. Police have registered an FIR against the accused and taken him into custody. Know the full story Sanjay Kumar, a labourer from Bhanipur village in Durgaganj police station area, works in Mumbai to support his family. His 12-year-old son Aditya, the only boy among his four children, had gone to Ambedkar Park, about 200 metres from his home, around 4 PM on Wednesday to watch a cricket match. He was sitting on the sidelines and was not playing. Around 5 PM, a 15-year-old batter was declared out but disputed the decision, claiming it was a no-ball. As the argument escalated, players asked Aditya for his opinion. When he said, 'It's not a no-ball,' the accused allegedly struck him repeatedly on the head with a cricket bat, leaving him critically injured and bleeding on the ground. Cousin also threatened with death According to eyewitnesses, after the incident, the accused threatened Aditya's cousin, who was with him, saying that if he reported the incident at home, he would also be killed. After this, he fled the scene. Father arrived to find son The cousin somehow managed to get home and informed the family about the incident. Upon receiving the information, father Sanjay Kumar reached the spot. The family first took Aditya to Sangam Hospital in Suriyawan, where he was referred after primary treatment. After this, doctors at Jeevandeep Hospital in Bhadohi city declared him dead at 8:28 pm. Upon receiving the information, Durgaganj police reached the spot. The police inspected the crime scene, collected evidence, and recorded statements of eyewitnesses and family members. He was supposed to go to Mumbai with his father today According to family members, the family's financial situation was weak. In search of better employment, the entire family was scheduled to go to Mumbai on Thursday by Kashi Express. Tickets were booked in advance, and preparations for a new life were underway, but this accident happened before that. Aditya was the only son of the family. He had one elder and three younger sisters. He had taken admission in class six this year and was enrolled in Madhaiya Inter College, Durgaganj. According to family members, he was bright in studies and was considered a great hope for the family. According to the police, the 15-year-old accused has been taken into custody and is being interrogated. The deceased's father, Sanjay Kumar, said, The children were playing cricket. A dispute arose over a no-ball. My son was just watching the match. He only said, 'It's not a no-ball,' when the boy who was batting hit him on the head with the bat. We run our family by working hard. Action to be taken after investigation CO Bhadohi CO Sumit Tripathi said In a dispute between two minor children, one child was seriously injured and died during treatment. Based on the complaint, a case has been registered and the accused minor has been taken into custody. Further legal action will be taken based on the investigation.

stories.title: Class 5 dropout dupes foreigners, earns ₹200 crore:119 call centre staff arrested, mastermind flees with girlfriend
stories.summary: One of the key accused in the cyber fraud syndicate operating under the guise of an international call centre in Lucknow is a class 5 dropout. The gang had rented two floors of the Summit Building for around ₹3 crore a year and employed 119 staff members, including men and women, who allegedly targeted foreign nationals. Police say the syndicate defrauded victims of nearly ₹200 crore in just one year. The main accused, Vineet Vashisht, who carried a ₹25,000 reward, was arrested on Wednesday along with his girlfriend Rinky Das Gupta and his associate Nayakar Jairaj from Kolkata. Police said none of the three arrested accused had studied beyond Class 10. Investigators said the trio threw their mobile phones into a river while fleeing Lucknow. They later booked a resort in Kolkata to hide, but were arrested there. ADCP Crime Kiran Yadav said that 119 accused were arrested during the raid on 1 July. Seven days later, police tracked down and arrested the alleged masterminds—Vineet Vashisht, Nayakar Jairaj and Rinky Das Gupta, from a resort in Kolkata. Police recovered an iPad, two Apple iPhones and ₹5,000 in cash from their possession. One discarded only the SIM card, leading police to the trio According to police, the three accused fled Lucknow immediately after the call centre was raided and travelled to Kolkata to evade arrest. Since Rinky is a resident of Kolkata, she was familiar with the area. Police said Vineet and Jairaj threw their mobile phones into a river while escaping. However, Rinky chose not to dispose of her expensive handset. Instead, she removed the SIM card, inserted a new one and used the phone to book a resort. That booking provided investigators with a crucial lead, enabling police teams to trace and arrest all three accused. What the accused told police ? Class 5 dropout, girlfriend studied till Class 9 During interrogation, Nayakar Jairaj told police he dropped out of school after failing Class 5. Rinky Das Gupta studied up to Class 9, while police are yet to verify Vineet Vashisht's educational qualifications. Investigators said Jairaj and Vineet had known each other for around 10 years after being introduced by a mutual friend. Rinky initially met Vineet for work, and the two later entered into a relationship. Nobody in the gang had ever met the alleged mastermind 'Charles' Police said the alleged mastermind behind the entire operation is a man identified only as Charles. Investigators claim that none of the gang members had ever met Charles in person. He remained in contact only with Vineet through WhatsApp calls and allegedly issued instructions remotely, which were then executed by the team operating from India. Victims' details shared through WhatsApp groups Police said the gang received details of targeted foreign victims through WhatsApp groups after calls were made overseas. Victims were allegedly persuaded to purchase gift cards or coupons. Once the coupons were scratched, photographs of them were uploaded to the WhatsApp group, allowing the gang to redeem their value. Investigators said a WhatsApp group named "Vendor" was used to circulate the targets' contact details, after which the Lucknow-based team contacted the victims. Fraud proceeds routed through hawala network The investigation found that Vineet Vashisht, Vikram Parmar and Lalit Kherajani alias Rodi allegedly operated the illegal call centre. According to police, Nayakar Jairaj arranged the office lease agreement, while Rinky Das Gupta handled the settlement of the fraud proceeds through hawala channels, both within India and abroad. Roles within the syndicate Police said Vineet, who is involved in the real estate business in Ahmedabad, financed the operation. Vikram Parmar and Lalit Kherajani allegedly managed the day-to-day functioning of the call centre, including recruitment and the execution of fraudulent transactions. Jairaj, an old associate of Vineet, held the office lease agreement in his name and allegedly received a share of the profits. Police said Rinky, Vineet's girlfriend, managed the hawala transactions. She also owns a salon and a bar named Toxic in Kolkata. ADCP Kiran Yadav said the investigation is continuing. Police are searching for other members of the syndicate and are attempting to trace the alleged mastermind, Charles.

stories.title: Akhilesh visits Shankaracharya to seek blessings:Second meeting in four months creates political buzz
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav met Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand in Lucknow on Thursday (9 July) morning to seek his blessings. He spent around 30 minutes with the seer and was seen sitting on the floor during the meeting. Speaking to the media afterwards Akhilesh said, “The Shankaracharya was deeply concerned about cow welfare and was exploring ways to secure national recognition for the cow.” Commenting on the alleged theft of offerings at the Ram Mandir he alleged, “Stealing devotees' offerings was a grave religious offence.” He accused the BJP of attempting to cover up the issue. He also claimed that there is growing unrest within the BJP, saying several leaders had already begun reaching out to him, and dismissed the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probe as a 'whitewash'. Shankaracharya questions government's response to alleged temple scam During the interaction, the Shankaracharya also questioned the handling of the alleged temple scam, asking whether the Chief Minister was taking action. He remarked that action was being promised but suggested meaningful steps would only be taken under a new Chief Minister. The seer is currently on an 81-day Gavidhi (Gorakshaarth-Dharmayuddh) Yatra to demand that cows be granted the status of "Rashtra Mata" (Mother of the Nation). He arrived in Lucknow on Wednesday and stayed overnight at the Jagan Lal Yadav Guest House in Faizullahganj. This was the second meeting between Akhilesh Yadav and the Shankaracharya in the past four months. Their previous meeting took place in Lucknow on March 12. Shankaracharya said - ‘Government considers cow as an animal’ Shankaracharya had a conversation with Akhilesh. During this, he was heard saying, “We took feedback from across the entire state. Asked whether you people consider the cow as an animal or mother, everyone said that we consider it mother. We told everyone that look, you people consider the cow as mother, but your government says that the cow is an animal”. 4 big points made by Akhilesh 1. BJP has distorted the dignity of Shri Ram Akhilesh said, “BJP's ideology changes for votes. For them, wealth is priority, not religion. Where are those who gave the responsibility? Where are those who had the responsibility? This is such a time that everything is on record. We can all see and understand.” He added, “At this time, Sanatanis across the world are worried. BJP has distorted the dignity of Maryada Purushottam Shri Ram in Ayodhya. Who knows what all they have done in their self-interest.” 2. Get the CDR of those working in the temple, 99% will turn out to be BJP people Akhilesh said, “FIRs are being filed against the opposition. Opposition's FIRs are not being registered. The people who used to work in the temple premises. CDRs of all of them should be extracted. 99% people will turn out to be BJP members. After that there will be a stampede in BJP, which you cannot imagine.” He added, “SIT is doing a whitewash. It has been heard that questions have been raised on SIT as well. One member has a case of 420 against him. This is a big fight. This is a Delhi-Lucknow fight. You are not able to understand.” 3. Action is being taken against SP MLAs to divert attention The SP chief further said, “The Delhi people get investigations done by ED, CBI and IT. Today you must have read in the newspaper that bundles of notes are coming out from someone's wall. To divert attention, action is being taken against SP MLAs”. He added, “Someone who has been in jail for many years, his place was raided. BJP should not bring such tradition and culture in politics that if someone goes to opposition, then attack them.” He further said, “This is a danger to democracy. Today they are in favor. Tomorrow they will also be in opposition. Put yourself in the place of opposition and see. You must have heard the language of the Chief Minister?” He stated, “When a suffering mother, sister and family members from Jaunpur went to meet him, what was his language like? When this is his language on camera, what must be the language behind the camera.” 4. CM went to Ayodhya so many times, but couldn't catch the theft On the question of appointing a CEO in the Ram Janmabhoomi Trust the SP chief said, “Not just the mold, the entire structure should be changed. Tell me, ethanol has been mixed in petrol. All the oil companies should issue s.” He added, “You mix 20, not 25 percent ethanol. Why aren't you mixing 30 percent? The companies that are making motorcycles and cars will have their scientific reasons. You are ignoring their scientific reasons. This is BJP's new kind of corruption.” On the question of whether CM is going to Ayodhya on 10 July he stated, “If he is going to Ayodhya, that's a good thing. He went so many times, still couldn't catch the theft. What will happen by his going? I have heard now that pickpockets are also active there.” 1 month ago Shivpal and Dimple Yadav took blessings from Shankaracharya A month ago, Shankaracharya's journey reached Saifai. At that time, SP's National General Secretary Shivpal Singh Yadav and Mainpuri MP Dimple Yadav welcomed Shankaracharya. They performed worship rituals and sought his blessings. Dimple Yadav said, “We are Yaduvanshi people. The cow has always been revered by us. We will do whatever we can to save it.”

stories.title: Ram Mandir donation theft probe widens:Police recover bundles of cash; freeze 30 bank accounts linked to accused's relatives
stories.summary: On Thursday morning, police took Ayodhya Ram Temple offering theft accused Anukalp Mishra to his house around 9 am, where they conducted a 20-minute search and questioned his family members. A day earlier, police had similarly taken co-accused Lavkush Mishra and Karunesh Pandey to their homes for searches. Authorities have frozen 30 bank accounts belonging to the accused's relatives after finding transactions disproportionate to their declared income. During the searches, police recovered bundles of cash, gold jewellery (including earrings and pendants), and a car from the three accused's houses. However, officials have not disclosed how much cash or which items were recovered from each residence. According to police sources, Anukalp told investigators that he and co-accused Avinash Shukla invested the stolen money in the stock market, lent it out on interest, and routed funds through relatives and close associates before transferring the money back into their own accounts. Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, speaking in Lucknow, said, Stealing temple offerings is a grave sin in our religion. They have committed a great sin. He alleged that the BJP was facing internal unrest and claimed the SIT was merely trying to cover up the case. He also questioned the SIT, alleging that one of its members faces a cheating case. On Wednesday morning, police had taken Karunesh Pandey, Anukalp Mishra, and Lavkush Mishra into 40-hour custody for questioning. Fake donation receipts were recovered from their possession.

stories.title: Shopkeeper stabbed to death in front of mother wife:Fight over parking tractor turns fatal in Gorakhpur
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, on Wednesday evening at 6 PM, a grocery shop owner was stabbed to death in front of his mother and wife. The mother kept pleading with the attackers, "Leave my son," begging with folded hands, but the attackers pushed her aside. The wife also arrived to save her husband from the attackers. She grabbed the attackers, but by then, 10 rapid knife blows had been struck into the shopkeeper's chest. He fell there, bleeding profusely. The attackers then fled the scene. The family took the injured shopkeeper to BRD Medical College, where doctors declared him dead. SP City Nimish Patil reached the spot and took information about the incident from the shopkeeper's son. Within a short while, the police arrested Gabbar Chauhan, who is accused of the stabbing. The incident is from Tikariya village in Gulriha, 15 km from the district headquarters. Now know the full case in detail Amarnath Gupta (56), a resident of Girmith Chauraha, was a grocery shop owner. His family includes his mother Janaki Devi, wife Gujarati Devi, two sons Rishikesh Gupta, Shivam Gupta, and daughter Priya Gupta. Adjacent to his house was the land of the accused, Avdhesh Chauhan alias Gabbar. Both parties were claiming ownership of this land. The dispute over this land has been ongoing in court for the past five years. On Wednesday evening, Amarnath parked a tractor in front of the same land. This led to an argument with Gabbar. Gabbar claimed the land as his own and refused to let the tractor be parked there. As the dispute escalated, Avdhesh Chauhan alias Gabbar Chauhan attacked Amarnath with a knife. Gabbar stabbed Amarnath about 10 times in the chest and stomach. At that time, Amarnath Gupta's mother, Janaki Devi, was present at the scene. She tried to stop the dispute. She was pushed and fell, sustaining injuries. Seeing her son being attacked, she started screaming and crying. Hearing her voice, his wife Gujarati Devi also came out of the shop. She pleaded with the attackers, but by then, they had committed the crime and fled. Son said father was sitting outside the house when the attack happened Amarnath Gupta's elder son, Rishikesh Gupta, said that Awadhesh attacked his father multiple times with a sharp weapon over a land dispute. He launched a deadly attack and murdered him. He stated that Mukund Chauhan, Aniket Surat, Bhane, Shailesh Jaiswal, and others were involved in this as well. At 6 PM, his father was sitting outside the house. Suddenly, these people came and attacked him. His 85-year-old grandmother, who came to defend, was also attacked, sustaining serious injuries in several places. Amarnath's lawyer stated that the accused was forcibly constructing on the victims' land, despite a court stay order. A dispute had been ongoing for the past 3-4 months regarding this matter. Force deployed in village, five people in police custody There was tension in the village following the killing. Police force was deployed to maintain law and order. Along with the main accused, four more people have been taken into custody. A case was registered on the complaint of Amarnath Gupta's son, Rishikesh. Police have filed an FIR against 10 named individuals, including the main accused Gabbar Chauhan, and seven unknown persons. SP City Nimish Patil said, There was already a dispute between both parties regarding land. The interrogation of the accused is being investigated. Further action will be taken based on the evidence.

stories.title: PM-Kisan 24th instalment explained:Avoid these mistakes to keep your ₹6,000 benefit
stories.summary: Farmers are now waiting for the 24th installment of the PM Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana. Under the 23rd installment, the government transferred ₹2,000 to the bank accounts of over 9.44 crore farmers. However, lakhs of beneficiaries missed out due to issues related to Aadhaar, e-KYC, bank accounts, or other technical glitches. Many eligible farmers have also not yet enrolled in the scheme. So, what should you do to ensure you receive the 24th installment on time? And what common mistakes should you avoid? Here's everything you need to know. Installment gets stuck due to 4 mistakes According to official data from the Ministry of Agriculture, the reason behind installment stoppage is not lack of budget with the government, but mismatch in farmers' digital records. Therefore, it is necessary to check these 4 things in your status- 1. Incomplete e-KYC- The government has made e-KYC mandatory to prevent fraud and fake beneficiaries. For farmers who have not verified their identity through face-authentication or OTP, the system puts their money on hold. 2. Not having a 'Farmer ID'- In UP, the benefit of PM Kisan Samman Nidhi will now only be available to those farmers who are registered on the 'Kisan Registry' portal. If your 12-digit Farmer ID has not been created, the money for upcoming installments may be withheld. 3. DBT and Bank Account not linked- PM Kisan money is not sent directly to the bank account, but through 'Direct Benefit Transfer' (DBT). For this, your bank account should be linked with Aadhaar. NPCI mapping should be active on it. 4. Farm not verified- Your farm details, i.e., Khasra-Khatauni, should be linked to your Kisan Digital Profile. If the verification of your land shows 'No' on the Lekhpal or Revenue Department portal, the installment will be stopped. Easy Way to Get Your Stopped Installment Back If your installment is stopped, you can fix it yourself from your mobile. After this, your stopped amount will be added to the next installment, i.e., ?2000 + ?2000 = ?4000 will be transferred. Do e-KYC Online- Visit the official website of PM Kisan pmkisan.gov.in. Click on the 'e-KYC' option on the right side. Enter your Aadhaar number. Submit the OTP received on mobile. Your e-KYC will be completed. You can also complete this process through face-authentication on the 'PM-Kisan Mobile App'. Link Bank Account with DBT- Visit your bank branch and fill the 'DBT/NCPI Mapping' form there. The bank employee will link your account with the government DBT server. Link Aadhaar Card with Agricultural Land- If land seeding shows 'No' on the portal, then meet the Lekhpal with a copy of your Khatauni. After verification, they will make it 'Yes' online. How Can New Farmers Join the Scheme for the First Time? The benefit of PM Kisan Yojana is only available to those farmers in whose name agricultural land was transferred before February 1, 2019. If land was received after this date, it will only be valid in cases where the name comes after the death of father or husband. Benefits are not immediately available on newly purchased land. If you have agricultural land in your name and are not yet availing the benefits of this scheme, you can do a new registration through the process given below. 24th Installment to Come in October-November According to the rules of PM Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana, the government gives farmers an installment of ?2000 at intervals of every 4 months. In this way, a total of 3 installments are released in a year. More than 23% of the beneficiaries are women. The first installment is released between April to July, the second between August to November, and the third installment between December to March. The 23rd installment has already been released on June 20. Therefore, according to the rules, adding 4 months' time, there is a strong possibility that the 24th installment will be released in October or November during the festival season. Where to Complain? If your status appears completely correct. In the system, e-KYC, Land Seeding, and DBT all show 'Yes'. Still, if the money has not reached your bank account, then you can directly contact the government's complaint cell- PM Kisan Toll-Free Helpline- 1800-115-526 or 155261 Official Email ID- pmkisan-ict@gov.in Local Resolution- You can also submit your written complaint by visiting the office of the Deputy Director of Agriculture in your district. Special counters have been set up here for every block. 4 Important Questions-Answers for Farmers' Work Question 1. Can both husband and wife avail the benefit of PM Kisan Samman Nidhi? Answer. No. According to government rules, only one member from one family will get the benefit of PM Kisan Yojana. If money is coming into the accounts of both husband and wife, then the government can also take back the amount later. Question 2. Will the family continue to receive installments after the farmer's death? Answer. No. The installment stops after the farmer's death. Another member of the family will first have to get the land registered in their name, then apply afresh. Question 3. What happens if the name is different in Aadhaar, Bank and Khatauni? Answer. If the name or spelling is different in all three places, then the PM Kisan installment may get stuck. Therefore, it is necessary to first make the name same in all records. Question 4. Can farmers who pay income tax avail the benefits of the scheme? Answer. No. Income tax payers, most government employees and people receiving monthly pension of more than 10 thousand rupees are not eligible for PM Kisan Yojana.

stories.title: 'Show me the document calling me Tipu':BJP MP replies to Akhilesh's defamation notice
stories.summary: The war of words between Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav and BJP MP Nishikant Dubey has escalated, with Dubey responding to the defamation notice served on him by the SP leader. On Wednesday morning, Dubey shared a copy of his legal reply on X, rejecting the allegations made in the notice and raising several questions for Akhilesh Yadav. Dubey questions 'Tipu' reference In his post on X, Nishikant Dubey wrote that he had already sent a reply to the legal notice. He questioned: Dubey further said he would seek compensation from Akhilesh Yadav's lawyer for the legal expenses incurred in the matter. Row began over social media post The controversy began after social media users claimed that Tinnu Yadav, one of the accused in the alleged Ram Temple donation theft case in Ayodhya, had been in regular telephonic contact with Akhilesh Yadav. On July 5, Nishikant Dubey shared an X post by Saravana Prasad Balasubramaniam, who claimed—citing police investigation and alleged mobile call records—that accused Tinnu Yadav regularly spoke with the SP chief. While sharing the post, Dubey wrote: Wasn't Tinnu speaking to Tipu? The remark triggered a sharp response from Akhilesh Yadav. Now read Nishikant Dubey's 4 posts Akhilesh threatened legal action Akhilesh Yadav demanded that Dubey delete the social media post within 10 minutes, warning that failure to do so would lead to a named FIR against the BJP MP. Calling the allegation false, Akhilesh said the BJP was attempting to malign the SP-led PDA alliance. He also referred to parliamentary decorum and the ideals associated with Lord Ram while criticising the post. SP sends defamation notice On July 7, the Samajwadi Party formally initiated legal proceedings by serving a defamation notice through Uttar Pradesh SP president K.K. Pal. The notice demanded that Dubey: Following the notice, SP workers staged protests against Dubey in Prayagraj, Etawah and several other cities. Complaints seeking registration of an FIR were also submitted to local police. Dubey defends his stand Responding to the notice, Dubey argued that under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Akhilesh Yadav himself would have to file a police complaint if he believed he had been defamed. Dubey also remarked that if the alleged defamation was against Akhilesh personally, the legal notice should have been issued directly in his name rather than through another party functionary. He further stated that he had been a member of the committee involved in framing the new criminal laws and therefore understood the legal provisions. Political exchange continues After Akhilesh threatened legal action, Dubey responded on X by saying: Go ahead. Why are you so worried? I only asked a question. Who ordered firing on Ram devotees in 1990? I will go to court. The exchange has kept the political confrontation between the two leaders alive for the past four days. SP leader challenges BJP to produce evidence Meanwhile, former SP MLA from Ayodhya, Pawan Pandey, released a video accusing the BJP, RSS and VHP of spreading false propaganda by linking Akhilesh Yadav to Tinnu Yadav through alleged phone calls. He challenged BJP leaders to produce evidence of any such conversation, failing which they should publicly apologise to Akhilesh Yadav. Pandey also said politics should be based on facts and evidence rather than false allegations, adding that he would quit politics if the BJP proved its claims. Who is Tinnu Yadav? Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu Yadav, currently lodged in jail, was formerly the driver of Ram Temple Trust General Secretary Champat Rai and is a resident of Ayodhya. According to the Special Investigation Team (SIT), Tinnu Yadav had access to the keys of the temple donation boxes (hundis) and related security arrangements despite having no formal written authorisation. The SIT report further stated that, on his recommendation, Manish Kumar Yadav was assigned donation-counting duties. Manish was later found allegedly involved in theft cases linked to temple donations. The SIT described the arrangement as a serious lapse in the temple's security and administrative system.

stories.title: Monsoon red alert in 27 UP cities:Ghaziabad roads flooded with two feet of water; 3 deaths reported
stories.summary: The monsoon is pouring heavily in UP. Since Thursday morning, it has been raining in 10 cities including Ghaziabad, Meerut, Bahraich, and Hapur. It rained so much in Ghaziabad that water accumulated up to 2 feet on the roads. Power supply was disrupted in several areas. Clouds have covered most cities including Lucknow and Ayodhya. Due to the rain, schools have been closed up to 8th grade in Mathura and Hathras, up to 9th in Meerut, and up to 12th in Ghaziabad. The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts today. Of these, 27 districts are on red alert, meaning there is a possibility of heavy rainfall in these districts. This is the first time a red alert has been issued this season. Speaking of Wednesday, it rained in 71 districts. In Prayagraj, two people working in a field died after being electrocuted. In Aligarh, a woman lost her life after being electrocuted in water. The highest rainfall of 144.4 mm was recorded in Chitrakoot. In the entire state, rainfall in the last 24 hours has been 46 percent above normal. Know about rain alert in Uttar Pradesh for today See pictures of the rain- Lucknow's meteorological scientist Atul Kumar Singh said- The rain system formed from the Bay of Bengal has now reached around Madhya Pradesh. Its effect is also being felt in UP. Therefore, the monsoon has gained momentum in the state. The spell of rain will continue for the next 5 days. Why is Uttar Pradesh likely to receive less rain this monsoon? According to India Meteorological Department (IMD) Director General Dr. M. Mohapatra, La Niña-like conditions in the Pacific Ocean are fading and signs of El Niño are emerging, which could lead to below-normal rainfall. This indicates that the southwest monsoon may remain weaker than usual this year. He also said that reduced snow cover in the Northern Hemisphere between January and March could affect the monsoon, further increasing the chances of lower rainfall in Uttar Pradesh. UP received 10–15% above-normal rainfall last monsoon According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Uttar Pradesh received an average of 870–900 mm of rainfall during the 2025 monsoon season (June to September). This was around 10–15% higher than the state's normal monsoon rainfall.

stories.title: 58-year-old police inspector falls for 35-year-old woman:'Marry me, I'll get you a job'; Bareilly woman alleges he forced her to abort
stories.summary: In Bareilly, a 58-year-old police inspector fell for a 35-year-old woman. The woman had come to the police station with a complaint about her husband, when the inspector told her - "Why do you worry, I am here. I will help you completely." After this, the inspector lured the woman with promises of a job and marriage and established a physical relationship with her. In 2026, when the woman became pregnant, he made her abort the child. When the woman asked him to marry her and make their relationship official, a conflict arose between them. The woman says - "I am an orphan, I have no one in this world. That's why I trusted the inspector, but he broke my trust. After living together for a year, he left me alone." On July 7, based on the woman's complaint, SSP Anurag Arya suspended Inspector Naresh Babu. Meanwhile, on July 8, the woman reached SP South Anshika Verma's office and recorded her statement. She provided photos and videos as evidence. The inspector is due to retire in 2 years. Dainik Bhaskar spoke with the woman. Read her story... 2 pictures of the inspector with the woman constable... ‘I needed support after separating from my husband’ The woman says, 'I am an orphan, I have no one in this world. I got married in 2022, but my husband tortured me a lot. After that, I started living separately from him. In the year 2025, I came in contact with Inspector Naresh Babu'.' She further adds, ‘I thought that the inspector was a good person. I needed support. But I did not know that the uniformed person I was trusting would turn out to be like this. He took advantage of my loneliness.’ ‘He assured to help me, then asked for my number’ I had filed a complaint against my husband at the police station. I met Naresh Babu several times regarding this. During this time, he took my mobile number by assuring help. He started calling me in the name of investigation. Instead of talking about work, he would talk about other things. After this, we also started meeting each other. Started living together at home from Karva Chauth The woman says, ‘In the year 2025, Naresh Babu told me that he had good relations with his Captain Sahab and that he will get me a job. He also promised to divorce his wife and marry me.’ She says, 'He assured me of marriage and started coming to my house. During this time, he had physical relations with me several times. I kept trusting the inspector's words because I believed he would marry me. After Karva Chauth last year, he started living at my house. We lived together in a rented room for about a year. He kept me as his wife. I even kept the Karva Chauth fast for him.' 'Took jewelry worth ₹8 lakhs on the pretext of son's wedding' The woman told that in February 2026, Naresh Babu took approximately ₹8 lakh rupees worth of gold jewelry from her, citing his son's wedding as the reason. Later, when she asked for the jewelry back, he started evading. When she protested, he began threatening me. The woman adds that after this incident Naresh Babu left her and went back to his wife and children. Inspector Naresh Babu has 3 children and grandchildren Naresh Babu, who lives in Shahpur, Moradabad, has been posted at several police stations in Bareilly. The inspector has one daughter and 2 sons. All three children are married. The inspector has grandchildren. In the year 2025, when he was posted at Baradari police station, the woman from Nai Basti had come to the station with a complaint of domestic violence against her husband. It was during that time that they both came in contact. The woman is a resident of Premnagar in Bareilly. She got married in Nai Basti, Bareilly in 2013. The woman lived with her husband till 2022. She also has a son who is 10 years old. The son lives with his father. The woman is divorced from her husband.

stories.title: Ram Mandir Trust to get corporate-style overhaul:Trustees prefer professional staff over IAS officers
stories.summary: The Shri Ram Temple Trust in Ayodhya has decided that the temple's day-to-day administration will now be overseen by a Chief Executive Officer (CEO). However, the trustees have ruled out appointing a serving IAS officer to the post, choosing instead to entrust the responsibility to a retired government official. According to a trust functionary, the decision was taken to ensure the temple remains administratively independent. The official said, “Appointing a serving bureaucrat could effectively place the temple's management under government control, whereas a retired officer would remain accountable only to the trust”. By contrast, several major temples, including the Kashi Vishwanath Temple and Ujjain's Mahakal Temple, have serving IAS or PCS officers as their CEOs. Three shortlisted candidates to be considered on July 22 The trust is expected to review a panel of three shortlisted candidates on July 22 and select one to serve as the temple's first CEO. Once the appointment is finalised, the trust will also define the officer's role, responsibilities and administrative framework. Staff structure will be created like a multinational company The Shri Ram Temple Trust now plans to manage the Ram Mandir on the lines of a multinational company. Under the proposed structure, a Chief Executive Officer (CEO) will function under the trust chairman, supported by engineers, financial experts and a workforce of around 1,500 to 2,000 employees. Staff appointed under this system will receive regular salaries. The CEO will also be paid a fixed salary. Until now, the trust's General Secretary Champat Rai and trustee Dr. Anil Mishra have been serving without remuneration. The trust also plans to make its functioning more transparent, allowing devotees to stay informed about its activities and administrative decisions. 'Dedicated professionals required to oversee operations' - Dev Giri Explaining the move, Shri Ram Temple Trust Treasurer Govind Dev Giri said, “The trust had not anticipated the need for professional management when it was constituted. However, following the recent donation theft case, dedicated professionals are required to oversee operations”. He added, “The CEO would report directly to the trust rather than the government, and the post would be filled by a retired IAS officer or a person with equivalent qualifications”. During the trust meeting held on July 6, members agreed that the temple's administration required closer monitoring and stronger institutional management. With only two trustees based in Ayodhya and most others residing in different cities and states, the trust believes a full-time CEO is needed to oversee the temple's day-to-day functioning and ensure continuity in administration. 3-member committee formed, it will select the CEO A three-member committee has been tasked with selecting the Shri Ram Temple's first Chief Executive Officer (CEO). The panel will submit a shortlist of three candidates to the trust by July 22, along with a detailed report outlining the CEO's roles and responsibilities. Whoever is appointed to the post will be expected to prioritise two key tasks. The first will be implementing the Special Investigation Team's (SIT) recommendations to prevent theft of devotees' offerings. The second will be strengthening the temple's security and surveillance system through the use of AI-enabled cameras and facial recognition technology. CEO to oversee daily operations, security and devotee services According to trust officials, the CEO's day will begin with offering prayers and taking darshan of Ram Lalla before assuming administrative duties. The role will include reviewing feedback from devotees, supervising ongoing temple construction and addressing the media on key developments. As the temple functions round the clock, the CEO will also be responsible for managing employee shifts and ensuring the smooth operation of all administrative and service-related activities. Truth Revealed in Audit Report SIT flags missing records despite ₹514 crore trust expenditure The Special Investigation Team (SIT) found major accounting lapses after examining the Shri Ram Temple Trust's financial records for the period between April 1, 2025 and March 31, 2026. During this period, the trust spent more than ₹514 crore, but investigators found that proper accounting records were not maintained. The report noted that several expenditure figures were based on estimates despite ₹16 lakh being spent on audit and legal fees. The SIT also found that ₹15 lakh was spent on travel without any record of whether the trips were undertaken by trust officials or employees. Similarly, expenditure of ₹2.59 crore under welfare activities and ₹2.71 crore under miscellaneous expenses lacked supporting details or documentation. The report further revealed that ₹11.49 crore was spent on security, yet theft of devotees' offerings continued to occur. It also questioned the utilisation of ₹1.84 crore spent on organising special events, noting that no records were available specifying what events had been conducted. Some other expenses shown in the report are as follows- Only 45 days video storage purchased for 66 lakhs, recommendation was for 180 days SIT questions CCTV policy after crucial footage found missing The SIT found that CCTV footage from the room where devotees' offerings were counted was automatically deleted after 45 days, despite the trust spending ₹66 lakh on video storage. The report noted that the trust's internal audit last year had recommended preserving the footage for at least 180 days, but the suggestion was never implemented. As a result, investigators were unable to retrieve older CCTV recordings during the probe, raising concerns over the loss of crucial evidence. Commenting on the issue, retired SP and cyber expert Triveni Singh said, “CCTV footage is generally preserved through cloud storage, with storage costs increasing as retention periods are extended”. He added, “Reserve Bank of India guidelines require cash-related recordings to be preserved for at least five years, while the Income Tax Department recommends retaining such records for up to seven years”. Now know about the Ram Mandir asset Temple trust holds 32 kg gold, ₹1,876 crore in bank deposits Since the construction of the Shri Ram Temple began, devotees have donated 32 kg of gold and 1,518 kg of silver as offerings. The trust sends the silver to the Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India, where it is melted and converted into 99.99% pure silver bricks before being returned. These silver reserves are stored securely in bank lockers. The trust also disclosed its financial position during the July 6 meeting. According to the figures presented, the Shri Ram Temple Trust has ₹1,876 crore deposited across accounts with SBI, Bank of Baroda and Punjab National Bank. The trust received ₹3,264 crore through the temple dedication fund during the construction phase, while offerings from devotees contributed another ₹582 crore. Of the total funds, ₹2,370 crore has been spent on temple construction and ₹391 crore on administrative and management expenses.
