stories.title: Why Ayushman and ABHA cards matter:Free doctor fees, ICU care and surgeries, ₹5 lakh treatment cover; know how to apply from home
stories.summary: To provide financial assistance to poor and middle-class families during illness, the government is running the Ayushman Bharat Yojana. In a medical emergency, free cashless treatment up to ₹5 lakh is available. It is essential that every eligible member of the family has an Ayushman Card. The government is also creating ABHA cards for people. This is a digital health ID where your health-related information is securely stored. Blood test reports, X-rays, and prescription slips are also stored online here. Free treatment in this health scheme The Ayushman Bharat Yojana belongs to the central government. It was launched on 23 September 2018. Under this, needy families suffering from serious illnesses receive assistance of up to ₹5 lakh for treatment. Expenses include everything from hospital admission to medicines, doctor's fees, ICU costs, and even operation costs. The government covers expenses from 3 days before admission to 15 days after discharge. Under this scheme, more than 1,900 serious diseases like cancer, heart disease, kidney failure, liver disease, cataracts, knee replacement, and bypass surgery can be treated free of cost. The benefit is available only if admitted to the hospital for at least 24 hours. Expenses for cold-cough or doctor consultation in OPD (Outpatient Department) are not included. To cover families whose names were not included in this scheme, the UP government launched 'Mukhyamantri Jan Arogya Abhiyan' on March 1, 2019. The entire process, from getting the card made to receiving treatment in the hospital, has been kept the same for both schemes. How to find out where to get free treatment The benefits of this scheme can be availed in all government hospitals and listed private hospitals across the country. Follow these easy steps to find Ayushman hospitals in your district. If you do not have internet, you can also call the toll-free numbers 14555 or 1800-111-565 to ask for the name and address of your nearest Ayushman hospital. Ayushman Vay Vandana Card for elders above 70 years Your Ayushman card contains your photo, name, date of birth, QR code, and an ABHA number. When admitted to the hospital, you only need to show this card. You can use this card for treatment in any state or city across the country. The Ayushman card made for elders aged 70 years and above is called the "Ayushman Vay Vandana Card". Through this, senior citizens of all categories, including General/OBC and SC-ST, can avail free treatment up to 5 lakh. This applies regardless of their financial status or whether they possess any other private medical insurance. Getting an ABHA card is also very important Just as a bank account keeps a secure record of your financial transactions, similarly, the Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) digitally secures your medical history. This 14-digit unique health ID is linked to Aadhaar. If you go to a hospital for treatment, showing your ABHA card there allows the doctor to know your health condition. This is because it contains records of all your medical reports, doctor's prescriptions, tests, and medicines. This helps in starting the correct treatment quickly and avoids the need for repeated tests. Government hospitals offer scan share facility with ABHA card. Scanning the QR code generates a digital slip. This eliminates the need to stand in long queues at the registration counter. How to correct errors in Ayushman Card If there is an error in your Ayushman card's name, photo, or other information, log in to the Ayushman App and click on 'Redo e-KYC'. After this, perform OTP or face verification again using Aadhaar. If online correction is not possible, contact the Ayushman Help Desk or Nodal Officer at your nearest district hospital. If you haven't made an Ayushman card, you won't be able to get free treatment worth ₹5 lakh in a medical emergency. Also, without an ABHA card, you will have to carry old reports and prescriptions every time. The doctor will not get information about your old illness or medicines, which can increase the risk of delay or error in treatment.

stories.title: Thar submerged, highway boundary collapses in UP:Rivers overflow bridges as rain lashes 10 cities, alert issued for 75 districts
stories.summary: Monsoon rains are lashing Uttar Pradesh, with rivers in western UP overflowing. In several places, water is flowing over bridges. Heavy rainfall was recorded in 10 cities, including Lucknow, Sultanpur and Ayodhya, at around 12:30 am on Saturday. Intermittent drizzle continued until early Saturday morning. Clouds are covering most other cities, while some areas have also witnessed sunshine. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain and hailstorm alert for all 75 districts for the next 24 hours. An orange alert for heavy rainfall has been issued in 13 cities, while 27 cities are under a yellow alert. In Bijnor, the Ganga and its tributary Malan River are in spate. Traffic on several routes, including the Meerut-Bijnor Highway and Haridwar Road, has been stopped after water reached the bridges. In Hapur, a Thar SUV got submerged after an underpass filled with rainwater. It was pulled out with the help of a JCB. In Meerut, the boundary wall of a National Highway collapsed. A car got submerged due to waterlogging at a railway underpass, trapping two youths inside. Police rescued both of them by pulling them out with a rope. Fifteen people have died in the state in the last three days due to rain-related incidents. Ghaziabad has reported the highest number of deaths, with four fatalities. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed officials to visit affected areas and ensure immediate compensation for victims. Four boys swept away in Bijnor, canal breaches in Muzaffarnagar Earlier, due to heavy rainfall, four boys were swept away in strong river currents in two separate incidents in Bijnor at around 4 pm on Friday. One has been rescued, while the search for the others is underway. In Saharanpur, soil from a cemetery was washed away, exposing bodies buried in graves. In Muzaffarnagar, an overflowing canal breached. Meerut’s Mawana records highest rainfall in 24 hours In the last 24 hours, the highest rainfall in Uttar Pradesh was recorded in Mawana, Meerut, at 315 mm. It was followed by Jansath in Muzaffarnagar, which recorded 270.1 mm of rainfall. Weather scientist Atul Kumar Singh said: The rain system formed over the Bay of Bengal has now reached around Madhya Pradesh. Its impact is being felt in Uttar Pradesh, due to which the monsoon has intensified in the state. The rainfall spell is likely to continue for the next 3-4 days. Most cities are expected to receive light to moderate rainfall, while several areas may witness heavy to very heavy rain.

stories.title: Rajpal Yadav gets 3-month jail term in cheque bounce case:Delhi HC orders ₹7.35 crore payout, wife fined; says 'Law is not a film script'
stories.summary: The High Court awarded Rajpal a three-month jail term in each of the seven cheque bounce cases against him. All the sentences will run concurrently. Justice Swarnakanta Sharma directed officials to send the actor to jail. Justice Swarnakanta Sharma observed that Rajpal Yadav's conduct was questionable. The court said he had been given several opportunities to honour his commitment and repay the company's dues, but failed to do so. It added that he would now have to spend the next three months in prison. The court also remarked that the law is not a script that an actor can rewrite according to his own wishes. Court orders Rajpal to pay ₹7.35 crore The High Court granted Rajpal Yadav two months either to comply with the order or challenge the sentence before the Supreme Court. The court directed him to pay ₹1.05 crore to the complainant in each of the seven cases, taking the total compensation to ₹7.35 crore. It also clarified that nearly ₹2 crore already paid by the actor would be adjusted against the total amount. The case dates back to 2010, when Rajpal Yadav borrowed ₹5 crore to produce one of his films. After failing to repay the outstanding amount and the cheques issued by him bounced, the dispute turned into a prolonged legal battle. Rajpal had said, 'I am ready to go to jail five times, but will not pay a single rupee' Advocate Avneesh Sikka, appearing for Murli Projects Private Limited in the Delhi High Court, said all 21 petitions filed by Rajpal Yadav had been dismissed and the Sessions Court's verdict had been upheld. Rajpal's wife, Radha Rajpal Yadav, was also an accused in the case. The High Court ordered her to pay a fine of ₹5 lakh in each case. During the hearing, Rajpal's counsel sought probation for the actor, but the court rejected the request, observing that he had repeatedly failed to honour assurances given to the court. The court also noted that during the final hearing, Rajpal had said, "I am ready to go to jail five times, but I will not pay a single rupee." Loan taken for film Ata Pata Lapata Rajpal Yadav had decided to make his directorial debut with the film Ata Pata Lapata. To finance the project, he borrowed ₹5 crore from Murli Projects Private Limited. The film flopped at the box office, leaving Rajpal unable to repay the loan on time. The unpaid dues eventually led to the long-running legal dispute. Got six months sentence in 2018 In April 2018, a magistrate's court convicted Rajpal Yadav and his wife Radha in the cheque bounce case and sentenced the actor to six months in jail. In early 2019, the Sessions Court also upheld the conviction. Rajpal has been to jail in a cheque bounce case In June 2024, the Delhi High Court stayed Rajpal's sentence temporarily and directed him to clear nearly ₹9 crore in outstanding dues. However, he failed to deposit the amount within the stipulated time. On February 2 this year, the High Court ordered him to surrender. Rajpal surrendered before Tihar Jail authorities on February 5, 2026. After spending 12 days in jail, he was granted interim bail by the Delhi High Court on February 17. Shahjahanpur children sent piggy bank money, Rajpal also came to meet them Several film personalities had come forward to support Rajpal Yadav financially. Actor Sonu Sood was among the first to offer help, while former Bihar Chief Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav's son Tej Pratap Yadav announced financial assistance of ₹11 lakh. Children from Gurukul Seva Trust in Shahjahanpur also broke open their piggy banks and collected around ₹10,000 to help the actor. About a month ago, when Rajpal visited Shahjahanpur, he met those children to thank them personally.

stories.title: Artist dressed as Lord Hanuman dances at BJP roadshow:Complaint filed in Chandigarh, alleges insult to deity
stories.summary: A controversy has erupted over a roadshow led by BJP President Nitin Naveen in Lucknow after an artist dressed as Lord Hanuman (Bajrangbali) was seen dancing while holding a BJP flag. On Monday at 12:55 pm, Advocate Vasu Ranjan, a lawyer at the Punjab and Haryana High Court and Chairman of the Council of Lawyers, sent a complaint by email to the Director General of Police (DGP) and the Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) in Chandigarh. The complaint alleges that during the roadshow, a person dressed as Lord Hanuman was made to dance in front of BJP President Nitin Naveen, hurting the religious sentiments of millions of Hindus. The complainant described the act as an inappropriate and disrespectful use of the sacred image of Lord Hanuman. He has demanded the immediate registration of an FIR against those responsible, an impartial investigation into the incident, and the preservation of all digital and other evidence related to the event. What the complaint alleges Lord Hanuman is one of Hinduism's most revered deities Advocate Vasu Ranjan stated in the complaint that Lord Hanuman is one of the most revered deities in Hinduism. He alleged that using the deity's sacred attire for political campaigning and propaganda amounts to a direct insult to the religious sentiments of devotees and constitutes a deliberate act of desecration. According to the complaint, the use of a revered religious symbol for political purposes is objectionable and has deeply hurt the sentiments of devotees. Alleged offence under Section 299 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita The complaint states that, prima facie, the incident falls within the scope of Section 299 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. According to the complainant, the provision applies to cases involving the deliberate insult of a religion or religious beliefs in a manner that hurts religious sentiments. He alleged that using the sacred image and attire of Lord Hanuman during a political roadshow falls under this provision. Demand for investigation into the role of organisers and leaders The complaint states that the incident took place in the presence of senior BJP leaders, including the party's national president and a chief minister. It therefore calls for an investigation into the role of the organisers, event managers, the person dressed as Lord Hanuman, and all individuals who allegedly authorised, encouraged or knowingly permitted the act. The complainant also urged the investigating agency to examine the conduct of every person present at the event, including the senior leaders. Demand for preservation of evidence and legal action The complaint seeks the immediate preservation of all electronic, digital, and documentary evidence related to the incident. It further demands that strict legal action be taken against anyone found responsible during the investigation, irrespective of their position or status, in accordance with the law.

stories.title: Akhilesh fumes over Ram Mandir allegation:Asks BJP MP to delete post in 10 minutes or face FIR
stories.summary: The alleged theft of donations from the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya has escalated into a political controversy after Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav strongly objected to attempts to link him with one of the accused, Ram Shankar Yadav alias Tinnu. The row began after BJP MP Nishikant Dubey, who represents Godda in Jharkhand, posted on X, suggesting that Tinnu Yadav had been in contact with Akhilesh Yadav. Reacting sharply on Monday evening, Akhilesh demanded that the BJP MP delete the post within 10 minutes, warning that failure to do so would result in a named FIR being filed against him. Akhilesh demands public apology In a statement posted on social media, Akhilesh said not only should the BJP MP remove the post, but anyone who had shared or amplified it should also delete it immediately and issue a public apology. He warned that legal action would be initiated against those who continued to circulate what he described as false information. Akhilesh alleged that the BJP and its supporters were spreading misinformation to defame the PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) community and asserted that the community would respond collectively. 'Delete the post or face legal action' Akhilesh said parliamentary privilege applies equally to both ruling and opposition MPs. Respecting what he described as the dignity of Lord Ram and parliamentary traditions, he said he was giving the BJP MP 10 minutes to delete the "false" post. "If the post is not removed, an FIR will be lodged immediately," he said, adding that BJP leaders would eventually have to face prolonged court proceedings and should not expect support from their political colleagues. He also accused the BJP of deliberately maligning the PDA community through misinformation. Why is Tinnu Yadav being linked to Akhilesh? Media reports recently claimed that Tinnu Yadav spoke with Akhilesh Yadav once or twice almost every day. Some reports further alleged that call records indicated Tinnu had spoken to the SP chief three times on the day before his arrest. However, there has been no official confirmation of these alleged call records or recordings. It also remains unclear why the conversations allegedly took place, what was discussed, or whether they had any connection to the alleged theft of temple donations. Earlier, after arrests were made in the donation theft case, Akhilesh had posted on X: The twig is punished, while the branch is forgiven. The remark was interpreted as suggesting that lower-level accused were being jailed while influential individuals were being protected. SP leader challenges BJP to produce evidence Former SP MLA from Ayodhya Pawan Pandey dismissed the allegations linking Tinnu Yadav to Akhilesh. He alleged that the temple donation theft had brought disrepute to the Ram Temple and blamed those associated with the Trust. Pandey challenged BJP leaders to publicly produce the Call Detail Records (CDRs) allegedly showing conversations between Akhilesh and Tinnu. He said that if such evidence was produced, he would resign from politics permanently. Otherwise, he demanded that BJP leaders stop making what he called baseless allegations against the SP chief. Akhilesh raises concerns over elections Speaking at a press conference in Lucknow earlier on Monday, Akhilesh also expressed concerns about the electoral process. Referring to allegations of vote manipulation, he remarked that there was now a fear that not only votes but even opposition candidates could be "stolen" or influenced. He urged party workers to remain vigilant and said the SP would discuss additional safeguards in future meetings. Targets BJP government on governance During the press conference, Akhilesh also launched a broader attack on the BJP government, accusing it of undermining public faith and engaging in internal power struggles. He alleged that: Comments on BJP, Uttar Pradesh politics and China Akhilesh also criticised the BJP over internal factionalism in Uttar Pradesh, claiming the party's legislators were attempting to change constituencies but asserting that the SP would instead replace them through elections. In a sarcastic remark, he described Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath as "a very good engineer," while blaming him for the design of Lucknow's ₹70-billion Green Corridor, alleging it had worsened traffic congestion. He further commented on national security, saying China had consistently posed the greatest threat to India's borders and accusing successive governments of remaining silent over repeated border incursions. The controversy over the Ram Temple donation theft investigation continues to fuel political exchanges between the BJP and the Samajwadi Party, with legal action now being threatened over allegations made on social media.

stories.title: Who is Krishna Mohan, new Ram Mandir Trust chief:Filed first donation theft FIR, joined RSS in 2012, became trustee 10 months ago
stories.summary: Just 10 months after being appointed as a trustee of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, retired IFS officer Krishna Mohan has reached the organisation’s most powerful position — the general secretary’s post. Krishna Mohan was appointed as a trustee in September 2025 following the death of Trust member Kameshwar Chaupal. After the alleged theft of offerings at the Ram Lalla temple came to light, Champat Rai resigned from the post of general secretary, creating a vacancy. Krishna Mohan, who has now taken charge of the post, is the same person who filed the first FIR on behalf of the Trust in the donation theft case. A 73-year-old member of the Dalit community, Krishna Mohan served as a 1977-batch Indian Foreign Service (IFS) officer. He joined the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) in 2012 and is currently the Kshetra Sanghchalak (regional head) of eastern Uttar Pradesh. During the Ram Mandir consecration ceremony in 2024, Krishna Mohan was among the yajmans who participated in the rituals. Krishna Mohan belongs to Hardoi in Uttar Pradesh Krishna Mohan is originally from Shahabad in Hardoi district of Uttar Pradesh. His father Dharmveer Singh worked with Indian Railways and has passed away. Krishna Mohan completed his MSc in Geology from Lucknow University. He has two brothers and four sisters. His younger brother Mahendra Singh is a doctor at Balrampur Hospital in Lucknow. Krishna Mohan married Kusumlata. The couple has a son, Saurav, and a daughter, Sneha Mohan, both of whom are married. His son Saurav works with the Postal Department in Lucknow, while his daughter Sneha Mohan is a government doctor in Noida. At present, the family of his driver lives at his house in Hardoi. Worked in Atomic Energy Department before joining IFS In the early phase of his career, Krishna Mohan worked for a few years in the Department of Atomic Energy. In 1977, he was selected for the Indian Forest Service (IFS) and served in the Maharashtra cadre. His long administrative experience in the service is considered to have given him strong management skills. Joined RSS after retirement in 2012 Krishna Mohan retired from government service in 2012 and later joined the RSS. Initially, he was appointed as the Nagar Sanghchalak of Hardoi. Later, he handled several responsibilities including: He is considered to have a strong image of being an honest and trusted person among the RSS leadership, BJP leaders and senior officials connected with the Trust. This credibility is believed to have helped him rise quickly to a key position. Why the general secretary post is considered the most powerful in Ram Mandir Trust In the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, the general secretary functions like the chief executive officer of the organisation. The post carries responsibility for almost every major operational aspect, including: Krishna Mohan faces challenge of restoring devotees’ trust After being appointed as acting general secretary, Krishna Mohan said that those accused in the donation theft case would be punished. He said the accused had taken advantage of management shortcomings and that these weaknesses would be removed to prevent such incidents in the future. He added that there was a sense of distrust among people and that efforts would be made to restore confidence. His statement highlights the biggest challenge before him — rebuilding trust after the controversy. However, he also faces several other responsibilities. Completing pending construction work The main structure of the Ram Mandir is ready, but several parts of the complex, including the museum, research centre, visitor facility centre, auditorium and other projects, are still under construction. Ensuring quality and completing these works within the deadline will be a major responsibility. Maintaining transparency in Trust functioning The Ram Mandir Trust receives donations from across India and abroad. Maintaining transparency in donations, expenses and audits will be one of the biggest challenges. Coordination with government agencies Krishna Mohan will have to maintain constant coordination with the central government, Uttar Pradesh government, Ayodhya administration, security agencies and construction companies. Developing Ayodhya as a global religious tourism centre Along with the temple, Ayodhya is being developed as an international religious tourism destination. Managing devotee experience, facilities and long-term plans of the Trust will remain a key focus area. Ensuring smooth leadership transition Champat Rai remained the public face of the Trust for a long period. Maintaining continuity after his departure and ensuring coordination among trustees will be another important challenge. Handling public and media scrutiny The Ram Mandir is one of the country’s most watched religious sites. Every decision of the Trust will remain under public and media scrutiny, making transparent and balanced functioning essential.

stories.title: Debt-ridden sweet shop owner jumps before train:Body dismembered; had borrowed ₹2 crore
stories.summary: A sweet shop owner allegedly died by suicide after jumping in front of the Farakka Express in Barabanki on Monday morning, reportedly due to a debt of ₹2 crore. The train dragged him for nearly 300 metres at around 9:30 am, leaving his body dismembered near the Banwa railway crossing, with his clothes completely torn. Police and Government Railway Police (GRP) reached the scene and sent the body for post-mortem. A motorbike (UP-41AY-2426) recovered from the spot was found to be registered in the name of the victim's neighbour, Himanshu Rastogi. The incident took place in the Jahangirabad police station area. See 3 pictures Complete matter in detail Anoop Gupta (40) was considered a big businessman in Barabanki. He owned a sweet shop named Krishna Sweets. His shop, located at the big intersection, was quite famous throughout the city. He lived with his wife Nidhi, daughter Bhavya (20), and son Manan (9). Anoop Gupta left home on Monday morning to drop his son at school. For this, he borrowed his neighbor Himanshu Rastogi's bike. After dropping his son at school, he did not return home. Around 9:30 AM, he committed suicide by jumping in front of the Farakka Express (number-15744) near the Banwa railway crossing. According to gateman Dharmendra and eyewitnesses, a young man arrived at the crossing on a bike. He parked the bike aside and stood near the tracks before the train arrived. As soon as the Farakka Express approached, he was hit by the train. The train was moving at high speed, so the young man was dragged for 300 meters. The body was torn into pieces. Daughter is state merit holder Anoop's daughter, Bhavya Gupta, secured the 18th position in the state's toppers list in the Intermediate examination. She is currently pursuing B.Tech from a university in Lucknow. Upon hearing the news of the incident, a large number of traders, relatives, people from social organisations, and family members reached the post-mortem house. Brother said - he was worried about his business Anoop's brother, Rajiv Gupta, said, In the morning, my brother went to drop his son at school, but did not return. Later, it was found that he had committed suicide by jumping in front of a train. He had been somewhat worried about his business these days. But, we never thought he would take such a big step. Rajiv Tandon, a close businessman of Anoop Gupta, said, Earlier Anoop used to run a grocery business. At that time, he had taken about two crore rupees on interest from moneylenders. With this money, about 6 months ago, he opened a sweet shop named Krishna Sweets at Bada Chauraha (Big Square). The shop was doing well. But, he used to say that the expenses were too high.Meanwhile, the moneylenders were demanding their money and interest back. Anoop was very troubled by this. He had told me these things many times. We used to explain to him that everything would be alright. Troubled by this, he jumped in front of a train today and took his own life. Meanwhile, Jahangirabad police say, The investigation of the case is being conducted with complete impartiality. The police are investigating the entire incident based on the post-mortem report, evidence collected from the crime scene, statements of eyewitnesses, and questioning of family members.

stories.title: 'Stepfather called me to maternal home to rape me':Daughter tells police; accused dies of heart attack at station
stories.summary: A man accused of raping his stepdaughter died during police questioning at Sidhauli police station in Shahjahanpur on Sunday night. The woman alleged that her stepfather had sexually assaulted her for the past three years, claiming he would even call her from her maternal home to rape her. Police said the accused's health deteriorated during questioning. He was taken to a Community Health Centre and later referred to the district hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The post-mortem report stated that he died of a heart attack. The death has raised questions over police action. The accused's family alleged he died at 1:40 am, while the FIR against him was registered at 2:19 am. Earlier on Sunday, the woman and her husband had filed a complaint at the police station. Police called the accused for questioning at around 3 pm, and he arrived with his wife. After an argument between the two sides, everyone else left, while the accused was detained for questioning. Questions on police FIR Around 1 am, the accused's health suddenly deteriorated. Police immediately took him to CHC Sidhauli, from where he was referred to the district hospital. Doctors at the district hospital declared him dead at 1:40 am. However, the FIR registered by the police states the time as 2:19 am. This raises the question of whether the FIR was written after the accused's death at night, following a complaint in the afternoon. Brother demands justice The deceased's brother has accused his niece and son-in-law of falsely implicating his brother. The brother says, We lived in the same house. My brother was very straightforward. He cannot do such a thing. We received this information at 1 am. When we reached the police station, my brother was not there. Upon going to the hospital, we found his body. Our family wants justice at any cost. Mother said that Daughter-son-in-law framed my husband The deceased's wife has also accused her daughter, son-in-law, and a middleman who arranged her daughter's marriage, of framing her husband. She said, After the daughter's allegations, the police took my husband to the police station. We left him at the police station and came home, but he died the same night. When the police took us back at night, my husband had already passed away. The CHC doctor said, Policemen brought a patient at night. His blood pressure had risen sharply to 210. The oxygen level was also not good. Considering it a case related to heart disease, the patient was referred to the district hospital for better treatment and ECG. SP Saurabh Dixit said, The FIR was registered at 12 o'clock. It takes some time for the FIR to be uploaded online. That's why there is a difference in time.

stories.title: 'Wife fights with me constantly':Man dies by suicide after recording video; says she should get nothing after his death
stories.summary: In Prayagraj, a truck owner, Arvind Tiwari (38), died by suicide by hanging himself at 1:30 am on Sunday. Before this, Arvind made a video. He forwarded it to his relatives on mobile. In the 49-second video, he accused his wife, father-in-law, and brother-in-law of fighting and quarreling. In the video, Arvind said, After I die, I want my wife to get nothing. Her father and brother, everyone fights with me. They don't make their daughter understand. They see flaws in me. I do everything. I give everything. Still, they say - what do you do? I tolerate it. My capacity to tolerate is very low. Therefore, there is no hope of living now. I want to die. Arvind also posted the video on social media around 1 am. After that, he tied a noose to a protruding rod from the roof of the house next door and took his own life. Around 2 am, when Arvind's mother came out, she saw her son's body hanging. She screamed. Hearing the noise, family members and people from the surrounding area gathered at the spot. They informed the police. The police brought the body down. Sent it for post-mortem. Questioned family members and neighbors. The case belongs to the Ghurpur police station area. Full incident details Arvind lives with his family in his ancestral house in Iradatganj. His father, Dayashankar Tiwari, has passed away. He used to run the family by driving a truck. After his death, Arvind continued the work. Arvind married Richa (34) 4 years ago. They have two children, an elder daughter aged 2 and a son aged 5 months. When his business went well, Arvind bought 2 trucks. Arvind himself drove one truck. Police said, Arvind lived at home with his mother, Shyama Devi (68), 3 brothers, wife Richa, and 2 children. On Sunday night at 12 o'clock, he had an argument with his wife Richa over something.He left the house in anger. He went outside and made a video at 1 am. He posted it on social media. He also sent it to his relatives. Then he made a noose out of a towel and committed suicide. ‘He used to help his brother, daughter-in-law did not like this’ At 2 am, mother Shyama Devi suddenly woke up. She got up, came out of the house, and saw her son Arvind hanging from a noose. Shyama Devi told the police that her daughter-in-law, Richa, used to fight with her son every day. He used to help his three brothers financially. All three brothers drive other people's trucks. Arvind wanted to give them his truck. Richa did not like this. Richa's father and brothers also used to trouble Arvind. For the past four days, Arvind was very disturbed. Wife says allegations are false Arvind's wife Richa, has denied the allegations. She said that minor arguments used to happen at home. The talk of harassment is wrong. The house is small. There is only one bathroom. Her husband's elder brothers use it. She used to object if it got late, which made them angry. There was also a slight argument at night. She thought he had left in anger and would return. But, his body was found. Ghurpur Police Station in-charge Atul Kumar Mishra said- The young man's mobile phone has been seized. The matter is being investigated. No complaint letter has been received so far. Further legal action will be taken after investigation into every aspect.

stories.title: DDU speeds up recruitment promotions:Ravi Kishan appointed professor of practice; 156 faculty elevated
stories.summary: Under the leadership of Vice-Chancellor Prof. Poonam Tandon, Deendayal Upadhyay Gorakhpur University has accelerated the filling of vacant posts and staff promotions through a transparent, impartial, and time-bound process aimed at improving education, research, and administration. Since the 2023–24 academic session, 156 faculty members have been promoted under the Career Advancement Scheme (CAS), including 42 Senior Professors, 6 Professors, 1 Associate Professor and 107 Assistant Professors. During the same period, the university also recruited 109 new faculty members- 27 permanent teachers (11 Assistant Professors, 10 Associate Professors, and 6 Professors) and 82 contractual Assistant Professors. The information was shared in a DDU Media Cell press release issued at 10:30 am on Monday. Students to gain practical knowledge from experts To provide students with practical and industry understanding alongside theoretical knowledge, the university has taken a new initiative by appointing three experienced experts as 'Professors of Practice'. Under this, Gorakhpur MP Ravi Kishan Shukla has been given responsibility in the Department of Fine Arts and Music, while renowned industrialists C.P. Agarwal and Atul Sarraf have been given responsibility in the Department of Commerce. Jobs for 14 employees In addition to teachers, the university administration has also made appointments to non-academic positions. Since September 4, 2023, 14 people have been given jobs under the compassionate appointment quota in various positions such as Junior Assistant and Attendant. Vice-Chancellor expressed confidence Vice-Chancellor Prof. Poonam Tandon said that having the right staff is most important for good education and better administration. She expressed confidence that with these new appointments, promotions, and the joining of experts, DDU will achieve new milestones at national and international levels under the New Education Policy.

stories.title: 80-year-old woman dies 35 days after being raped:Accused entered victim's home to commit assault when she was alone
stories.summary: An 80-year-old woman in Uttar Pradesh’s Hathras district has died after being hospitalised for 35 days following an alleged case of sexual assault. The woman, who had been undergoing treatment since the incident, died around 12:30 am on Sunday night during treatment. According to police, a 35-year-old man named Salman allegedly entered her home on the night of May 31 and assaulted her after finding her alone. He then fled the scene, leaving her unconscious. The incident came to light the next morning when neighbours found her house door open. She was discovered in a seriously injured condition and was later admitted to a district hospital before being referred to a medical college. Although there was some improvement in her condition, she was later shifted back to the district hospital, where she eventually passed away. Police had arrested the accused shortly after the incident and registered a case under relevant sections following a complaint lodged by a neighbour. A medical examination had confirmed the assault. Officials said the post-mortem examination of the body will be conducted, and further legal sections will be added to the case based on the report.

stories.title: VIDEO | SI manhandled by truck driver:Claims policeman stole ₹20,000 from his truck while taking lift
stories.summary: A truck driver allegedly thrashed a sub-inspector in Hamirpur in broad daylight on Monday around 9:30 am after accusing the police official of stealing ₹20,000 from the truck's cabin. According to the driver, the incident began on NH-34 when the officer reportedly took a lift in the truck near Ghazipur (Ghata Khand area). Near the Aliyapur toll plaza under Sajeeti police station limits, the sub-inspector allegedly took ₹20,000 from the truck cabin and fled in a van. The driver pursued him for nearly 13 kilometres and eventually caught up with him near the Yamuna bridge. He then grabbed the officer by the collar and allegedly assaulted him repeatedly on the highway. In the video that has surfaced, the driver is seen delivering multiple slaps within seconds, while the officer’s uniform is torn during the scuffle. The driver further claimed that when he pulled the officer’s uniform, the allegedly hidden cash fell out. Following the incident, the sub-inspector, identified as Girish Mishra, posted in court security duty in Hamirpur, has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been ordered by the Superintendent of Police. An FIR has also been registered against him at Sajeeti police station on the complaint filed by the driver. Details of the case According to truck driver Manish, he was returning after selling gravel when he picked up sub-inspector Girish Mishra near Ghata Khand area of NH-34, mistaking him for a regular passenger. The journey remained normal until the vehicle reached near the Aliyapur toll plaza under Sajeeti police station limits, where the driver claimed he discovered ₹20,000 missing from the cabin. The driver alleged that the officer had concealed the cash inside his uniform and, when confronted, got down from the truck and fled in a van. Manish said he did not give up and chased the vehicle for nearly 13 kilometres. After crossing the Yamuna bridge, the officer reportedly got off the van and started walking, where the driver finally caught him. On searching him, the driver claimed the missing ₹20,000 was recovered, following which he lost his temper and slapped the officer two to three times on the roadside. A large crowd gathered on the highway after seeing a uniformed police officer being assaulted. Locals intervened and informed emergency police response service UP-112. The officer was taken to the local police station. A video of the incident was also recorded and later went viral on social media. Circle Officer Yashpal Singh said that based on the viral video and complaint, a case has been registered at Kotwali Nagar under relevant sections. The sub-inspector has been suspended with immediate effect, and a departmental inquiry has been ordered. Further action will be taken based on the findings of the investigation.

stories.title: Truck rams 2 traffic constables, one dead:Erring truck driver dies while trying to escape from the scene
stories.summary: In Kanpur, on the Barra Elevated Road, at 4 AM on Monday, two traffic constables on duty were crushed by a truck. One constable died on the spot. The other is seriously injured. After the accident, in an attempt to flee, the erring truck driver tried to drive away but he lost control and crashed into a container truck moving ahead. In this, the truck driver also died. The collision was so severe that the truck's cabin was crushed. The driver's body got stuck in the cabin. The body was removed by cutting the cabin. The deceased Jitendra was a constable of the 2018 batch. He was originally from Agra. While constable Rakesh Kumar is injured. He has been admitted to Kashiram Hospital. Rakesh is originally from Bulandshahr. The truck driver has not been identified. Constables were going to clear a traffic jam when accident occurred According to the police, both constables Rakesh and Jitendra were on duty at Naubasta Bypass. Information was received that there was a traffic jam on the elevated road. Both left on a bike from Naubasta towards Barra Elevated Corridor. As they reached the elevated road, suddenly a speeding truck hit their bike. As soon as they were hit, both constables fell to the ground. The container crushed Jitendra and moved forward. After the accident, the truck driver panicked. He started speeding the truck on the elevated road itself. A little further ahead, he crashed into a container. He died in it. Elevated Road remained jammed for 2 hours As soon as the news of the constable's death in the accident was received, Additional Commissioner of Police (Law and Order) Dr. Vipin Tada and DCP Traffic Ravindra Kumar reached the spot. They inspected the accident site. Information was gathered regarding the causes of the incident. After the accident, traffic remained jammed on the elevated road for about 2 hours. See 3 pictures of the accident... Constable Jitendra Kumar's brother Khyali Ram said - I run a salon in Agra. Brother Jitendra's marriage took place on December 2, 2020, with Varsha, daughter of Kailashchandra, a resident of Etawah, who was posted in PAC. They have a two-and-a-half-year-old daughter, Bhumika. Father Veerdharam used to do labour work. The family includes mother Phoolwati and five sisters. The sisters are already married. Jitendra's brother-in-law Keshav said the information about the accident was given by a traffic constable living near the village. Jitendra was living in a rented house in Nirala Nagar with his wife and daughter since his marriage.

stories.title: Wife allegedly dies by suicide after husband cancels flight ticket:Dowry murder case registered against 5; husband in custody
stories.summary: The death of a newly married woman in Lucknow has led to a dowry murder case against her husband and five members of his family. The victim, Sonali, had been married for just four months and was found dead under suspicious circumstances at the couple's rented flat in Shivajipuram, Indiranagar. According to police, Sonali and her husband, Kamalakant, originally planned to travel to Kashmir by flight. However, Kamalakant, a deputy manager at a private bank, cancelled the flight tickets and booked train tickets instead. The change reportedly upset Sonali, leading to an argument between the couple. Although the dispute later subsided, Kamalakant left for work as usual. When he called his wife from work, she did not answer. He then asked the landlord to check on her. The landlord found the flat locked from inside and discovered Sonali hanging. She was later declared dead. Sonali was a resident of Kharharad Simri in Bihar's Buxar district, while Kamalakant belongs to Pinjaroi village in the Sandesh area of Bhojpur district. The couple had married in February this year and had been living in Lucknow. Following a complaint by Sonali's family, police registered a case of dowry murder against Kamalakant and five members of his family. The husband has been taken into custody for questioning. Sonali's brother, Abhishek Ojha, alleged that the husband murdered his sister and that her in-laws, including her mother-in-law, father-in-law, elder brother-in-law, elder brother-in-law's wife and sister-in-law, had been mentally harassing her over dowry demands. He further alleged that Kamalakant photographed Sonali's body to make the death appear to be a case of suicide. Husband says, ‘He sent train ticket on WhatsApp before calling’ During police questioning, Kamalakant said that due to work commitments, he and his wife had not been able to go on a honeymoon after their marriage. A month ago, they planned a trip to Kashmir and booked flight tickets. Sonali arrived in Lucknow on 28 June. On Friday, he cancelled the flight tickets and booked train tickets instead. Sonali became upset, leading to an argument between them. On Saturday, he went to work as usual. From there, he sent the train ticket to his wife via WhatsApp. He said that when he later called her, she did not answer. After several unsuccessful attempts, he asked the landlord to check on her. The landlord found the door locked from inside. Kamalakant then rushed home and found Sonali hanging inside the room. Family arrives from Bihar, FIR registered On Sunday, Sonali's family arrived in Lucknow from Bihar. Based on their complaint, police registered a case of dowry murder against the husband and five members of his family. The family alleged that Sonali was repeatedly harassed over demands for a car and cash. They claimed she had come to Lucknow on 28 June to stay with her husband and that he killed her on 4 July before trying to present it as a suicide. They also alleged that he took photographs with the body before informing the family. The victim's family submitted the photographs to the police, alleging that instead of taking Sonali to hospital immediately, the husband first posed for photographs with her body. Brother alleges harassment over dowry demands Abhishek said that on Saturday night, his brother-in-law called to inform him that Sonali had died by suicide and had been taken to hospital, where doctors declared her dead. He alleged that ever since the marriage, the husband and his family had been demanding a car and cash. According to him, Sonali was continuously insulted and mentally harassed by her husband Kamalakant, mother-in-law Ramawati, father-in-law Shardanand, sister-in-law Girija Choubey, elder brother-in-law Laxmikant and elder brother-in-law's wife Laxmi. Family says, ‘₹15 lakh cash and furniture worth ₹2.5 lakh were given at marriage’ In his complaint at Indiranagar police station, Abhishek stated that the bride's family had spent lavishly on the wedding. They gave ₹15 lakh in cash and furniture worth around ₹2.5 lakh. Despite this, he alleged, the husband's family continued to harass Sonali and repeatedly demanded a car. Dowry murder case registered; husband in custody Based on the complaint, Indiranagar police registered a case of dowry murder and other relevant offences against the husband and five members of his family. Police have detained the husband for questioning. Senior officers said the post-mortem report lists the cause of death as hanging. They added that the investigation is continuing on the basis of other available evidence.

stories.title: Man kills girlfriend for refusing to show WhatsApp chats:Body dismembered; accused arrested after police encounter
stories.summary: In Jaunpur, a young man murdered his married girlfriend on Saturday by slitting her throat for not showing her WhatsApp chat. He cut the body into three pieces with a billhook. He severed both hands and both legs. He filled the hands and torso in black polythene bags and threw them in bushes along the roadside at different locations. On Sunday morning at 6 AM, people out for a walk became suspicious due to a foul smell. When they went closer, they saw polythene bags. Upon receiving information, the police arrived and opened the polythene bags, finding the woman's torso. When they started searching for the remaining parts, hands were found one kilometre away. 3 teams were formed to search for the remaining parts of the body. The entire area was cordoned off. Meanwhile, late on Sunday night, an informant reported that a person was carrying similar black polythene bags on a bike. Around 12:30 AM, the police surrounded him. Fearing capture, the accused opened fire. In retaliatory action, the accused was shot in his right leg. He fell on the road. Police arrested him and took him to the hospital. The woman's leg, the axe used in the crime, and a pistol were recovered from him. During interrogation, he confessed to the crime. The woman was identified as Reshma Khatoon alias Sana (38) from Varanasi. Her husband has identified the body. The incident took place 25 km from the district headquarters in the Madiyahun Kotwali area. Understand the entire case in a sequential manner- Woman's legs, mobile recovered from accused Police recovered a knife, a cleaver, a .32 bore pistol, cartridges, the woman's severed legs, a bike, and the woman's mobile phone used in the crime from the accused. A case has been registered against him under various sections including murder, destruction of evidence, deadly assault on police, and illegal possession of weapons, and further legal action has been initiated. Woman has three children, family lives in Varanasi The accused told the police that Sana was married. She has three children. The eldest son is 20 years old. The two daughters are 19 and 14 years old. She was married to Rahim Khan, a resident of Kewalipur, Varanasi. CO Vijay Chaudhary said- Accused Dilip has been arrested. He had an argument with the woman, after which this incident occurred. The woman's husband, Rahim Khan, has identified her. The body has been handed over after post-mortem. Rahim will also be interrogated.

stories.title: UP's Jalalabad to be renamed Parashurampuri:Yogi cabinet approves name change after Centre's nod
stories.summary: A Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was held in Lucknow at 10 am on Monday. The Cabinet approved 28 proposals, including the renaming of Jalalabad in Shahjahanpur district to Parashurampuri. Cabinet Minister Suresh Khanna said Jalalabad is believed to be the birthplace of Lord Parashuram. The Uttar Pradesh government had sent the proposal to the Central Government on 25 June, 2025. After receiving a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Centre, the Cabinet approved the name change. Another major proposal provides cashless medical treatment of up to ₹5 lakh for Uttar Pradesh Home Guards and their families. The state currently has 1.18 lakh Home Guards. In addition, the recruitment process for 41,000 Home Guards has been completed. As a result, more than 1.60 lakh Home Guards and their family members will benefit from the scheme. The cabinet also approved the establishment of an ESIC Medical College in Varanasi. Fifty per cent of the seats at the medical college will be reserved for the children of workers. Details of cabinet decisions: 1. Uttar Pradesh startup mission directorate to be established The Yogi Cabinet approved the establishment of the Uttar Pradesh Startup Mission Directorate, the UP Startup Policy-2026, and the Data Centre Policy. The Chief Secretary will head the Mission Directorate. An Empowerment Committee will also be formed. A Startup Fund of ₹1,000 crore has been created, including ₹400 crore from AKTU. 2. Livestock insurance scheme approved for animal rearers The Cabinet approved the Chief Minister Risk Management and Livestock Insurance Scheme for livestock owners across all 75 districts of the state. Under the scheme, the state government will bear 85% of the insurance premium, while livestock owners will contribute 15%. Cabinet Minister Dharampal Singh said the scheme will reduce the financial burden on farmers and livestock owners. The insurable value of livestock has been fixed as follows: The minister said there are currently around 1.35 lakh cattle in government cow shelters across the state, with nearly ₹8 crore being spent daily on their upkeep. The insurance premium will be shared as follows: Insurance benefits will be available if an animal dies due to natural disasters, disease, or accidents. 3. ESIC hospitals for workers in Gorakhpur and Moradabad The Cabinet approved the construction of 100-bed ESIC hospitals for workers in Gorakhpur and Moradabad. It also approved free land allocation for establishing an ESIC Medical College in Varanasi. Cabinet Minister Anil Rajbhar said five acres of land each have been allotted for the hospitals in Gorakhpur and Moradabad. The medical college in Varanasi will be built on 13 acres of land. Half of the seats at the medical college will be reserved for workers' children. Out of 50 seats, 25 will be reserved for them. 4. Direct government recruitment for international medal winners The Cabinet approved amendments to the Direct Recruitment Rules-2022 for international medal-winning athletes. The state government will now be able to appoint international medal winners directly without requiring them to undergo the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC) selection process. Cabinet Minister Girish Yadav said the provision applies to medal winners at the Olympics, Women's Olympics, Asian Games and other international sporting events. The policy will apply to Group 'A' and Group 'B' government posts. Direct recruitment will be made for: Bronze and silver medal-winning athletes will be eligible for appointment. 5. First private agriculture university to come up in Kanpur The Cabinet approved the establishment of three private universities in Uttar Pradesh: The Cabinet also approved the allocation of 20 hectares of land and ₹50 crore for establishing a Horticulture College and Research Centre in Raebareli. stories.title: Ruchi Veera on BJP defection buzz:'Show the evidence'; says Kamal Akhtar should follow Akhilesh's order
stories.summary: The conflict between SP MP from Moradabad, Ruchi Veera, and SP MLA from Kanth, Kamal Akhtar, is in the headlines. To end this dispute, SP President Akhilesh Yadav stripped Akhtar of the post of Chief Whip of the legislative party. Despite this, the matter does not seem to be cooling down. Meanwhile, news of Ruchi Veera joining the BJP has spread rapidly. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Veera on speculations of her joining BJP. She said, “If anyone has any proof, present it. My ideology never aligns with BJP. I am a soldier of SP, and will remain with the SP until my last breath.” On the conflict with Kamal Akhtar, Ruchi Veera said, “They (Kamal Akhtar and his supporters) should heed the message Akhilesh-ji has given them.” Veera answered candidly on questions ranging from factionalism in SP to efforts for former MP Azam Khan's release. Read the full interview Question- What is the real reason for the conflict between you and Kamal Akhtar? Answer- There is no question of conflict. I am an MP and he is an MLA. I don't have to contest the MLA election, so there won't be any conflict. That episode is now over. There are many people in the party, so there can be differences, but there is nothing significant like that. Question- Akhilesh had reconciled you and Kamal Akhtar, but the situation hasn't changed? Answer- If there is any issue, we should inform our leader. Every party has minor issues. I have no personal conflict with him. Nor is there any conflict over land, property, or business. With (state) elections approaching, we should keep meeting the leader. If anyone is still making statements, it is wrong. When the episode was closed and the national president resolved it, there should be no more statements. Question- Kamal Akhtar even helped you contest elections. Your relations were good, so why such a conflict? Answer- I am a loyal soldier of the SP. Including me in any programme will only add some votes. I don't think this was such a big issue. The BJP has blown it out of proportion through the media. Appearing in a photo at an event, or having my photo on a poster or not, is not a big deal for me. I live in people's hearts. I don't need to be on posters. Question- It is being said that you want to field your daughter from the Moradabad Nagar seat, which is why there was a conflict? Answer- Let anyone in Moradabad tell me if I ever said that I want to field my daughter from here. This could be misinformation. This could also be a BJP plan. I have said before that my daughter never had, nor will ever have, any intention of contesting elections from Moradabad district. Question- It is being said that you are in contact with BJP and might join BJP? Answer- Let anyone provide such proof... My ideology does not align with the BJP. My father-in-law has been a MLA three times and a minister. I have a secular mindset. Yes, some small-time people are writing that guidelines have come from the center for 37 Samajwadi Party MPs. I want to tell these people to at least leave the family members and loyal people alone. Neither am I in touch with anyone, nor can anyone prove it. BJP and BJP MLAs are scared of my popularity. The way I stay among people in every joy and sorrow, because of that, I have become a challenge for BJP MLAs. Question- By making your photo with the Speaker viral, it is being said that you are joining BJP. Answer- Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla ji had come to Moradabad last year. It is my responsibility that if the Speaker of my house has come to my constituency, I should at least welcome him with a bouquet. This is both my responsibility and my right. As a local MP, I had welcomed the Speaker. This picture is from that time. In politics, this courtesy is a common thing. Question- You had talked about sidelining a woman MP in the party, are you not given time? Answer- Whenever I ask for time, I get time from the party leadership. It might be a day or two earlier or later. He (Akhilesh) is a former Chief Minister and a future Chief Minister. He has a busy schedule, but my leader also gives me time and listens to me. Question- Who will benefit from the conflict between you and Kamal Akhtar? Answer- BJP wants to capitalize on this. The strength with which SP is entering the election arena has disturbed BJP's sleep. In the last general election, SP won 37 seats in UP. We are people who struggle. SP is a struggling party. There is no sabotage here. BJP should not dream Mungerilal's beautiful dreams. Everyone will unite to defeat BJP and make Akhilesh Yadav the Chief Minister of UP again. Question- Azam Khan is your political guru. What efforts did you make for his release after becoming an MP? Answer- Whatever is happening with Azam Sahab, it has not happened with any leader in independent India. He is a very big secular leader. Azam Sahab has dedicated his entire life to SP. Everyone has benefited from the university he built. He is being targeted. He is not a criminal. I and all SP leaders want Azam Sahab to come out and guide us in the elections. But, the government has decided not to let him out. Fighting with the government is difficult, but we are confident that justice will surely be served one day. Question- Is SP moving towards soft Hindutva? Answer- The first thing is that whether it's Akhilesh Yadav's family or us, we all are followers of Sanatan Dharma and Shankaracharya ji. The position of Shankaracharya has always been respected. Even in the past, if a king was wrong, Shankaracharya would instruct him and work on correction. But, the government is now not ready to accept his correct words. All of us and our party's leader are followers of Sanatan. What's new in this, they have always been revered. Question- What message do you want to give to Kamal Akhtar? Answer- Who am I to give a message? The message has been given by the National President ji, follow that. I would only say that we have to fight against BJP. We don't have to fight among ourselves. It's possible that some people's mutual views don't align or we have our own ambitions, but the party is supreme for us. If the government is formed and Akhilesh becomes the Chief Minister, then the strength of all of us will increase. In such a situation, we will be able to serve people with more strength. Question- What do you have to say about the theft of offerings at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya? Answer- It is a great misfortune for the country. It is an attack on the faith of people of Sanatan Dharma. First, these people benefited from Ram's name, and now they are stealing Ram's donations. This is a big robbery. The government should resign. You are playing with people's faith by stealing from the temple of the very deity because of whom you are in power. An investigation should be conducted by forming a committee of a sitting judge. Justice cannot be expected from a Special Investigation Team (SIT) in this matter. Now understand why the dispute between the MP and the MLA occurred? Actually, SP MP Ruchiveera is upset about not being invited to the 'PDA conference'. She believes that MLA Kamal Akhtar was behind this. However, Kamal Akhtar says that he worked hard for Ruchiveera in the Lok Sabha elections, considering her as his sister. The PDA conference, to which she claims not to have been invited, took place on the occasion of Amjad Pathan being made the Metropolitan Vice President. The event was organized on June 14 by Rajya Sabha MP Javed Ali in the Moradabad Rural assembly constituency. Find out next, what happened in the Lucknow meeting MP-MLA clashed in front of Akhilesh According to sources, there was a heated argument between MP Ruchi Veera and Kamal Akhtar in front of Akhilesh Yadav during the meeting. Ruchi Veera alleged that she was not invited to party programs and her photo was not put on posters. Meanwhile, Kamal Akhtar alleged that he was not invited to the Mushaira and Azam Khan's birthday program organized by Ruchi Veera. There was also a lot of debate regarding another person, Khushnood, who was present at the meeting with Akhilesh. Khushnood, present at the meeting, was speaking in favor of Ruchi Veera. Kamal Akhtar objected to this and said - Javed Ali is an MP, Madam is also an MP, I am an MLA, is Jaiveer the district president? Who is this? What is his work here? On this, Ruchi Veera said- This is Khushnood and he has come with me. Then Kamal Akhtar said- We also have many people outside with us, should I call them too? As the dispute escalated, Akhilesh Yadav stopped Kamal Akhtar and Ruchi Veera and asked Khushnood where he was from? Khushnood said that he was from Bijnor. Then Akhilesh said that when I call the people of Bijnor, then you speak. After this, Ruchi Veera also asked Khushnood to remain silent.

stories.title: Farmer ID now mandatory in UP:No fertiliser or seeds without it; know how to apply online via mobile
stories.summary: The UP government is preparing a 12-digit unique ID for farmers, calling it 'Farmer ID' or 'Kisan Registry'. The ID will record information related to farmers' land and the amount of farming being done on it. This ID will be mandatory to procure fertiliser, seeds and even to avail government schemes like PM Kisan Samman Nidhi, crop insurance, Kisan Credit Card, and loan waiver. The government claims that this will ensure that the benefits of schemes reach needy farmers and fraudulent practices are stopped. Complete farm data in Farmer ID Farmer ID is a digital database, in which the farmer's name, Khasra-Khatauni (essential land record documents) data, and information about the crop sown in the field will be digitally recorded. After the Farmer ID is created, when a farmer goes to get fertiliser, the Farmer ID will be scanned. This will let the system know how much land the farmer has. How many bags of fertilizer he needs. This will ensure that eligible farmers receive the correct amount of fertilizer. It is often observed that when there is a shortage of fertiliser, black marketing begins. Some people hoard stocks of urea or DAP. In such a situation, the Farmer ID will curb black marketing. Registered farmers will receive benefits of PM Kisan Samman Nidhi According to the UP government, farmer IDs have been created for about 75 per cent of the state's farmers. This means that out of 2.4 crore farmers, the digital registration work for over 1.8 crore has been completed. A special campaign is being run to connect the remaining farmers. After this, the Agriculture Department will make the Farmer ID mandatory in schemes related to fertilisers, seeds, pesticides, and other agricultural materials. The selection of beneficiaries for the schemes will also be done based on the Farmer ID database. In the future, installments of PM Kisan Samman Nidhi will also be given only to those farmers who have a Farmer ID. It has also been decided to make Farmer ID mandatory in schemes of Horticulture, Animal Husbandry, Fisheries, Cooperatives, and Sugarcane Development departments. No need for repeated registration at centers Currently, farmers have to register anew every season to sell crops like paddy and wheat at government procurement centers. After the creation of the Farmer ID, this hassle will end. By entering the ID, information about the farmer and their land will appear. It takes a lot of time to get a Kisan Credit Card (KCC) due to land documents and verification. With the Farmer ID, this process will become digital, which will help in getting loans quickly. What is the last date to get a Farmer Registry made? The campaign to create Farmer Registry in UP has been ongoing since 2024. Initially, it was started as a pilot project, but in 2025 and 2026, it was run in mission mode. The government first set its last date as April 30, then extended it to May 15, 2026. Currently, registration is ongoing and a new last date has not yet been decided. However, from June 1, 2026, Farmer Registry has been made mandatory for government agricultural schemes. Contact here for help or complaints If there is an error in the name, Khasra number, or land record in the Khatauni, there may be problems in creating the Farmer ID. Therefore, the revenue records will have to be updated first. If a farmer wants to register a complaint related to any agricultural scheme, including PM Kisan, they can contact the government helpline 0522-2317003 or the toll-free Kisan Call Center 1800-180-1551. For complaints, the Chief Minister's helpline 1076 can also be contacted. 5 Important Questions Related to Farmer ID Question 1. Will there be any fee for this ID? Answer. No. Jan Seva Kendra (Public Service Center) may charge ₹20 to ₹50 for filling the form, uploading it to the computer, and e-KYC. Question 2. What are the rules for sharecroppers (tenants)? Answer. The Farmer ID of tenant farmers can be created after the consent of the landowner. Both will undergo digital verification. After the Farmer ID is created, tenant farmers will also be able to sell their crops at MSP. Subsidies for fertilizers and seeds, crop insurance, and compensation benefits will also be directly deposited into their bank accounts. Question 3. Can the tenant farmer misuse this? Answer. Land ownership does not change with farmer registration. The tenant farmer receives consent for only one crop season. The landowner can withdraw their consent at any time if they wish. Question 4. How will the ID be created in the case of a joint account? Answer. Even with a joint land record (khatoni), a separate Farmer ID will be created for each account holder in the family. The ID will be linked to Aadhaar and e-KYC. If the share is recorded in the land record, benefits like fertilisers, seeds, and others will be received in the same proportion. If the share is not recorded, benefits will be determined based on digital crop survey and actual cultivation. Question 5. Can Farmer ID data be used in cyber fraud? Answer. stories.title: Ram Mandir Trust accepts Champat Rai's resignation:Krishna Mohan named New General Secy; trust expresses shame over theft
stories.summary: In the ongoing controversy over the alleged embezzlement of donations at the Ayodhya Ram Temple, the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has accepted the resignations of General Secretary Champat Rai and trustee Anil Mishra. Retired IFS officer and trustee Krishna Mohan has been appointed as the acting General Secretary, replacing Champat Rai. The trust's first meeting after the theft lasted nearly three hours. Addressing the media afterwards, Treasurer Govind Dev Giri said, Champat Rai felt it was not appropriate to remain in office until the culprits were arrested. What happened is deeply painful. We are all saddened by it. The donation theft is a shameful incident. During the meeting, trustee K. Parasaran said the trust's constitution provides that a resignation is deemed accepted as soon as it is submitted, which is why both resignations were accepted. Krishna Mohan said those responsible for the donation theft would be brought to justice. He added that the accused had taken advantage of shortcomings in the trust's management, and those gaps would now be addressed to prevent such incidents from happening again. He also said the trust would work to restore public confidence, which had been affected by the controversy.

stories.title: Heavy rain floods Bareilly as 57 cities remain on alert:Roads flooded, e-rickshaws overturn; monsoon to strengthen from Tuesday
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh has witnessed highly variable weather since the onset of the monsoon. Intense heat has persisted during the day, with spells of rain accompanied by strong winds. Bright sunshine after showers has pushed up humidity levels. Most cities, including Lucknow, Bareilly and Kanpur, have been experiencing strong sunshine with intermittent cloud cover. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a thunderstorm and rain alert for 57 cities on Monday (6 July), along with a warning of lightning. According to the IMD, a weather system over the north-west Bay of Bengal is expected to cross the north Odisha coast by Monday evening and move towards Chhattisgarh. Its interaction with the existing western disturbance could trigger sudden heavy rainfall in parts of Uttar Pradesh, with hail also possible. The monsoon is then expected to strengthen across the state from Tuesday. At around 1 am on Sunday, Bareilly witnessed heavy rain accompanied by strong winds. Several roads were waterlogged, with flooding persisting until morning. A number of e-rickshaws overturned in the water. During the day, intermittent rain was recorded in 18 cities, including Lucknow, Varanasi, Prayagraj, Ghaziabad, Ballia and Jalaun. Lucknow and Barabanki also experienced rain accompanied by strong winds. According to the IMD, Uttar Pradesh received 67.7 mm of rainfall between 1 June and 5 July, against the normal of 125.6 mm for this period. This means the state has so far recorded 46 per cent below-normal rainfall this monsoon season. Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said: The weather system near the north Odisha coast has influenced weather conditions in Uttar Pradesh, causing the monsoon to weaken temporarily. Light rain is occurring in some districts due to local weather systems. Humidity and heat have increased across eastern and central Uttar Pradesh. The monsoon is expected to regain strength within the next 24 hours, after which rainfall activity will intensify across the state. Monsoon Meter Note: Data is up to 5 July 2026. stories.summary: In the Ayodhya Ram Mandir offering theft case, Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust's General Secretary Champat Rai and member Dr. Anil Mishra remain outside the purview of the police investigation. In such a situation, the big question is whether these senior officials are guilty or not? According to legal experts, two charges can be levelled against them. First is concealing the crime. Second is that though they were in important positions in the trust, they were unable to detect the crime that was happening right under their nose. Trust officials were informed about the theft on 4 June 2026. On June 5, cash was recovered from the residences of some suspicious employees. On June 7, Champat Rai released a video, in which he stated that no theft had occurred. On June 25, eight people associated with the offering and cash counting process were named in the FIR. This determines that it was an attempt to conceal the crime. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to senior lawyers regarding this case. Senior lawyers of the Ayodhya Bar Association said, “Senior office bearers of the trust will come under legal scrutiny. They cannot escape”. Another senior lawyer said, ”The name of a trustee has come up in the statements of the accused. It is certain that responsibility will be fixed when new names emerge in the police charge sheet." Lawyers says senior officials will get into trouble for not informing the police Senior advocate Ashutosh Tripathi, associated with the Ayodhya District Bar Association, said, “The role of the senior office bearers of the trust is suspicious. They may come under legal scrutiny. When the information about the theft was received on 4 June itself, then who was hiding it for 20 days?” The law states that as soon as information about a crime is known, the police should be informed. The facts of the offering theft were hidden from the police. Therefore, the office bearers of the Ram Mandir Trust become accused under Section 61 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). This section deals with criminal conspiracy. A case can be registered against the trustees for involvement in the crime. 'Trustees are seemingly guilty of criminal breach of trust' Ayodhya's senior lawyer Kalika Mishra says- The responsibility for the security of offerings in the trust lay with the office bearers. It has come to light that the theft came to their knowledge. Yet they did not take the right steps. Section 316 of BNS (Criminal Breach of Trust) states that if a person, who has property entrusted to them, misappropriates it or allows someone to steal it, then they are guilty of criminal breach of trust. This can lead to a sentence of up to 10 years. Police officers investigating without authority will also be implicated Upon receiving information about the theft of offerings, some police personnel deployed for the security of Karsevakpuram or Ram Mandir violated the Right to Duty and Service Rules. They, without any FIR or search warrant, acting as 'third parties', started searching for items at the suspects' homes. Such police personnel can be suspended under the 'Right to Service'. The senior officers of the department should have submitted a written report on this. It should also be investigated under whose pressure they conducted such an investigation beyond their authority. Accused may get 'benefit of doubt' Ayodhya lawyers believe that the trust's attempt to suppress the case and recover money from the homes of various suspects without any authority could weaken the entire case in court. 1. Police will get stuck during testimony- When testimony takes place in court and the investigating officer or the case's sub-inspector is asked, 'Did you recover this money?' and he denies, 'No... a certain person brought it.' Then the question will arise as to by what authority that money was taken? 2. Accused will get the benefit of doubt- Due to non-compliance with the process and a delay of 20 days, the accused may legally get the 'benefit of doubt', which could lead to their acquittal. Should statements of Dhirendra Shastri and Brijbhushan Singh also be recorded? Senior advocate Ashutosh Tripathi said, “Whispers of theft have been circulating since the land fraud came to light, suggesting something was amiss within the temple and trust.” Recently, statements from two prominent figures of the country on this matter - Dhirendra Krishna Shastri (Bageshwar Dham) and Brijbhushan Sharan Singh - have emerged. Both hinted This is a very big matter, I will not take names. Whoever stole Lord Ram's money, they will finish me off too. This raised the question of who is such an influential person, whose fear is so great? The SIT and the investigating officer should take cognisance of these two major statements and issue summons to them. They should be questioned about what information or evidence they have, which they are refraining from stating on an open platform. Lawyer says, ‘If Champat becomes an accused, he will justify himself’ Former Additional Advocate General of Lucknow, Raghavendra Pratap Singh, has a slightly different perspective. He believes that it is difficult for the heat to reach senior officials, because the matter is not of dishonesty but of 'betrayal'. He said, “In this matter, some corrupt people got close to Champat Rai. This is a direct 'betrayal' of 20 years of trust. When someone of your own betrays you, what can a person do? As for the delay, usually when a servant steals in the house, the owner first tries to interrogate and recover the goods himself, and only later goes to the police.” Know the Legal Hurdles in the Case Role of Trust officials not clear The accused include Champat Rai's driver (Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu), the General Secretary of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, and contractual employees associated with the counting room. The counting room and keys were with them. So far, only junior employees have been caught. Until the 'banking and security failure' that occurred under the supervision of senior trust officials is added to the FIR or charge sheet, the accused can avoid major charges by portraying it merely as departmental negligence. Digital evidence is very important in this case So far, ₹79.85 lakh and foreign currency have been recovered from the accused. Under the new criminal laws (BNS/BNSS), the chain of digital and forensic evidence must be extremely strong. If concrete evidence (such as CCTV footage or audit matching) directly linking the recovered cash to the specific theft from temple donation boxes is not presented in court, the accused can complicate the case by claiming the mere recovery of money as their private property. Secret presentation, procedure not followed Several local lawyers have objected that the police presented the accused before the remand magistrate in a very secretive manner. If the necessary legal procedures or timelines for arrest and remand were not fully followed, it could become an issue of 'illegal detention', making it easier for the defense to obtain bail. The lack of legal aid for the accused also provides an advantage The Ayodhya Bar Association has decided not to fight the case of the accused. Article 22(1) of the Indian Constitution grants every accused the right to be defended by a lawyer of their choice. According to the instructions of the Supreme Court, if an accused does not receive fair legal representation, the entire trial of the lower court cannot be considered valid. This technical ground may be sufficient to quash the conviction or overturn the case in the High Court. Ram Temple Offering Theft: Highest Recovery Made from Avinash Note: US$112, two gold chains, one ring, and silver ornaments were also recovered from Avinash.
